The $120 Floor Lamp T1 is a rod-shaped light with a wall-wash effect. It has 18 controllable zones that can be set to different colors, with support for 2000K to 9000K white light at up to 1,000 lumens.

$66 for a 10-foot strand, with 16-foot and 32-foot options available as well.

title: iFixit Says Apple's HomeView is Unnecessarily Hard to Repair
content:
iFixit today tore down the Apple HomeView to see what's inside, and found that the device takes a step backward in repairability compared to the HomePod. Getting into it resulted in damage to internal components.



Strong adhesive holds the HomeView's display in place, and iFixit said it was difficult to remove. There's a mix of Phillips and Torx screws in different sizes securing internal components, necessitating several tools.

Speakers take up most of the internal space behind the display, with the logic board located behind them. The logic board has a shield that connects to the back of the aluminum enclosure, turning the entire thing into a heat sink to improve thermal performance. The thermal paste and adhesive attaching the shield to the casing made the logic board difficult to remove.

The speakers are held in place with a thick adhesive pad, and attempting to remove one caused it to snap in half. There are multiple cables connecting the display to the speaker base, and iFixit found the components of the wall-mounted and tabletop versions of the HomeView aren't interchangeable. The devices have different internal designs, with the wall-mounted version using a larger logic board and the tabletop model adopting larger speakers and a pivot mount.

The HomeView speaker base is designed similarly to a ‌HomePod‌, and iFixit found it easier to take apart. The USB-C port on the base is modular and can be replaced, as can the two passive speakers inside the enclosure. Because of how the HomeView is assembled, it isn't possible to separate the display from the base without going through the display side.

title: Final Cut Pro Now Includes MotionVFX for Creator Studio Users
content:
Apple today updated Final Cut Pro (FCP), adding MotionVFX integration. Apple purchased the company earlier this year, so now the MotionVFX library is part of FCP. It includes the templates, titles, themes, effects, layouts, and transitions that are popular with creators.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

MotionVFX graphics and effects can be dropped into a video timeline, and 3D titles and graphics can be added to a scene on moving surfaces or at a natural depth that matches camera movement. Masking improvements make it quicker to add outlines, accents, motion trails, and more to video subjects, and static photos and illustrations can be turned into animations.

There's a new Content Hub with access to stock video, photos, graphics, and backgrounds. Creators can also generate images in FCP with text descriptions, and then edit those images. Any image from an FCP project can be opened in Pixelmator Pro for editing, and then added back to FCP when editing is finished.

Apple added easing options for more precise control over animation, and there's a new timeline command for detaching a clip from the primary storyline to reposition it freely without affecting B-roll, titles, and audio.

The new features are included in the Creator Studio version of Final Cut Pro, so you will need a Creator Studio subscription to use them. Creator Studio is priced at $12.99 per month and includes access to Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Motion, Compressor, and special features in free apps like Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

The one-time purchase version of Final Cut Pro does not include the new additions.

Update: Apple's outage today has delayed the release of the Final Cut Pro update, but it should be out shortly.

title: Welp, it’s Apple’s turn: iCloud and other services are struggling to stay online today
content:
Macworld





The past week has been a nonstop parade of important network outages, from a big Microsoft fiasco to the FAA grounding planes and more, including network issues at the NSA and JPMorgan Chase & Co. Now, it looks like it’s Apple’s turn.
For the last couple of hours, several of Apple’s network services have been experiencing problems. The System Status page has shown various services in various states of operation, from iCloud Mail to Apple Music and News, though most of them have returned to “green” status. Several internal Apple networking services for employees are said to be affected as well.
At the time of this writing, there are scattered issues with some of the School Management services and AppleCare’s on-device signup, volume purchases, and the App Store. It is not clear how widespread these issues are, however, and two of our editors in the U.S. were able to use the App Store just fine, for example.
In a statement to Bloomberg, Apple said, “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible.” Apple also said the problems do not stem from a cyberattack, echoing the sentiment from Microsoft and others. Apparently it’s just been a really bad week.

title: macOS 27.3’s new Full Disk Access prompt protects your data from apps that want it
content:
Macworld





In October, Apple announced that it was going to change how it implements Full Disk Access control in macOS. Users were going to have to perform “very explicit user action” to grant FDA to an app, which is a change from before, when apps could prompt users to flip switches on in System Settings to allow FDA.
The change is coming to macOS 27.3, and it was recently unveiled in the macOS 27.3 beta 2 that was released on Monday. Apple released a note to developers notifying them about the change, stating that the changes “empower [users] to make informed decisions about their own data and privacy.”
The new FDA UI was posted online by madeby_ldt, and it’s much more detailed and explicit. When an app asks for FDA, users will now be able to see what data the app wants to collect and grant permission to certain types of access. For example, the ChatGPT app wants access to be able to “Read, Change, Delete, and Export All Your Data,” “View Hidden and Recently Deleted Photos,” and “View History and Browse as You.” You’ll be able to allow or deny access to each of those requests.


macOS 27.3 now warns you before giving an app full disk access
That warning prompt is pretty scary! pic.twitter.com/J2qCKVWJRx
— ldt (@madeby_ldt) November 16, 2026





The example provided uses ChatGPT, which is no coincidence. Chatbots and other AI apps want as much access to your data as they can get—it’s how they function and are able to tailor responses to your specific needs. AI apps aren’t the only ones that want FDA, but they grow more popular every day, and a lot of users are naive about how they work. Apple’s changes to FDA are one way to bring awareness of AI demands to the user.
Apple is expected to release macOS 27.3 in early December. Keep track of the latest with macOS 27 in our superguide.
creator: Macworld

title: Apple Moves Ahead With Better Dual SIM Support for Apps
content:
Apple is moving ahead with changes that could make it easier to use separate work and personal numbers in third-party iPhone calling and contact apps, after advancing a request to the development stage this week.


The request was submitted by developer Airelec Clima on August 9 and would let these apps use more of the information iOS already keeps about a user's two cellular lines.

Today, third-party apps lack a supported way to read the names users give their cellular lines, such as "Work" and "Personal," or read and change the preferred line saved for each contact in iOS. The proposed changes would make that information available to eligible apps.

For example, someone could use a third-party contact app to choose their work number for calling a colleague. Apple's Contacts and Phone apps would then share that preference. The third-party app could also display the user's familiar "Work" and "Personal" labels, making it easier to tell the two numbers apart.

The developer also wants apps to be able to tell which line was used for a call in call history, where that information is available. This could let an alternative calling app show whether an incoming call came through the user's work or personal number.

The request does not seek access to sensitive SIM identifiers or subscription credentials. The developer says apps would only need the line's label and an identifier that tells one cellular service apart from another.

EU interoperability process, which lets developers ask for access to iPhone and iPad features used by Apple's own apps or hardware. Apple operates the process to help meet its obligations under the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA).

requires Apple to give third parties access to the same operating system features available to its own services and devices, so competing products can work as seamlessly with the platform. Although this request falls under the EU process, the resulting changes could be made available more widely.

title: X-VPN’s Talaria Protocol: What the Speed Gains Mean on a Mac
content:
Macworld





		
Test X-VPN's new speed boost for yourself for free
Combined download and upload improvements of 200%
Learn more
A VPN encrypts your traffic and sends it through another server, which usually costs some speed. The speed upgrade built around X-VPN‘s new Talaria protocol reduces that speed cost, and its published tests include impressive Mac results. (A protocol is the set of rules a VPN uses to connect and encrypt your data.)
What is Talaria?
Talaria is X-VPN’s in-house, open-source VPN protocol. It is available on macOS, Windows, iOS and Android, for Free and Premium users, and you need the latest version of the app.

				
					

				
			
X-VPN




How much faster is it on a Mac?
X-VPN’s macOS tests used an Apple M4 Mac mini on a wired connection.
On a 10Gbps connection, median download speeds (the middle result across repeated tests) rose from between 543 and 753 Mbps with X-VPN’s previous Everest-UDP protocol to between 3,661 and 5,437 Mbps with Talaria, depending on the server.
On a 1Gbps connection, Talaria kept 98.2% to 98.7% of the download speed measured without a VPN, a loss of 1.3% to 1.8%.
X-VPN’s headline figure is an overall improvement of over 200%. That averages combined download and upload improvements across its wider 10Gbps test set, covering Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, so it isn’t a Mac-only number.

				
					

				
			
X-VPN




Where will Mac users notice it?
Downloading large files. X-VPN says Talaria reduces download times for things like 4K films and system updates. If you keep the VPN on during a big download, that is where waiting time should drop. X-VPN gives no figure for the reduction.
Using a fast home connection. On a 1Gbps plan, the 98% result means most of the speed you pay for stays intact with the VPN on.
Running several apps at once. Say you’re streaming, downloading and browsing together. Talaria gives each app connection its own data channel, so the streams can run side by side. On macOS, X-VPN also controls how much work runs in parallel, which keeps processor cores productive and reduces competition for shared resources.
Working on a multi-gigabit connection. Few homes have a 10Gbps line, so the 10 Gbps results matter mostly for offices, labs and enthusiasts.

				
					

				
			
X-VPN




What else is behind the speed gains?
X-VPN credits the improvement to the whole connection, not the protocol alone. On the server side, it says more than 90% of its traffic in the US and Europe can be served by 10Gbps or 25Gbps infrastructure. Its current bare-metal servers (physical machines rather than shared hosting) run 64 processor cores.
On your side, the app tests available high-capacity entry points and weighs the available bandwidth, to pick a route suited to current network conditions. X-VPN also streamlines how data moves through the app, reducing copying and repeated work.
Is Talaria secure?
Talaria uses TLS 1.3, hybrid post-quantum key exchange (designed to resist future quantum computers) and separate keys for each connection and direction. Its code has been public on GitHub since October 16, 2026. Vantage Point Security independently assessed it and found no vulnerabilities in the reviewed scope. That assessment covers security, not speed.
What are the limits?
These are X-VPN’s internal tests, run from August 22 to September 8, 2026, from a single starting location. The Mac tests used one machine on a wired connection, and mobile tests used Wi-Fi. X-VPN says results vary by device, server, route and network conditions, and not every optimization applies to every platform.
Because Talaria is available on the free plan, you can try it and see how it performs on your own connection. X-VPN notes that performance varies by plan, platform and connection.

title: Former Apple Chairman Plans to Sell $32 Million in Apple Stock
content:
Apple's former chairman Arthur Levinson plans to sell 90,000 Apple shares worth approximately $31.8 million, according to a new filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.


The shares are held in Levinson's trust and were originally acquired in February 2001, more than 25 years ago. The filing lists November 16 as the expected sale date, but does not confirm whether the transaction was completed.

Apple stock traded at around 35 cents per share on a split-adjusted basis at the time. At that price, the shares being offered for sale would have cost approximately $31,500, compared with their value of nearly $32 million in the filing, which is roughly a thousandfold increase. 

Tim Cook became executive chairman and John Ternus took over as CEO. Levinson remains on the board as lead independent director.

title: Apple Accused of Silencing iPhone Duo Supplier Over 'Crackgate' Issue
content:
Apple allegedly pressured a component supplier to withdraw a public statement distancing itself from the display cracking issue affecting some iPhone Duo units, according to The Elec.


The allegation surrounds the little-known Fine M-Tec, which reportedly supplies internal metal plates supporting the iPhone Duo's folding screen. Last month, the Korean-based supplier published a statement denying that defects in its components were responsible for the reported display failures. 

The Elec reports that Fine M-Tec posted "Our official position on the customer's new product quality issue" on its website on October 26. The statement read: "The quality issues that are known to have occurred in some products recently are not caused by quality defects in the parts we supply." Fine M-Tec said it published the statement to counter accusations associated with suspected short sellers. It also warned of possible legal action against those spreading unsubstantiated claims.

This statement, which did not outright name Apple or the iPhone Duo, appeared shortly after the first cases of hinge-related screen damage on Apple's first foldable began to emerge online.

DealSite reported that its industry sources suggested the supplier had been pressured by Apple to remove it.

published Tuesday, The Elec journalist Kim Geon said a Fine M-Tec representative had since contacted him requesting the removal of his earlier article about the withdrawn statement. According to the representative's account, Apple had objected to the supplier publicly denying responsibility for the failures.

acknowledged display cracking affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units and offered replacements, but the company hasn't offered a technical explanation for what is causing the issue. Meanwhile, Apple has not publicly commented on the allegation that it pressured a supplier into silence.

title: iPhone relatively safe while the rest of the smartphone market contracts
content:
The global smartphone market is getting hit hard by global economic factors paired with RAM and flash storage pricing, but standing out from that drama is the expectation that iPhone shipments will grow 7% in 2027.

iPhone Duo
In a research report published November 16, Morgan Stanley estimated that Apple will ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027. Worldwide smartphone shipments are expected to decline 5% to 1.04 billion units, following an estimated 13.8% contraction in 2026.
The forecast is a substantial downgrade from Morgan Stanley's previous expectation of 3.6% industry growth in 2027. The bank attributes the weaker outlook to rising component costs and a lack of compelling reasons to upgrade.
Rising memory prices remain a major concern for smartphone manufacturers. Apple has already warned that memory costs are climbing rapidly, leaving manufacturers of cheaper smartphones with less room to absorb the increases.

title: Apple HomeView: Everything you need to know about Apple’s smart-home display
content:
Macworld





Apple HomeView is Apple’s first dedicated smart-home display, combining a 7-inch touchscreen, powerful speakers, a camera, and Siri AI in a device designed to sit at the center of the connected home. Announced on October 13, 2026 and on sale from November 13, it brings together smart-home controls, entertainment, video calling, calendars, reminders, and other everyday information.
Powered by Apple’s A18 chip and Apple Intelligence, HomeView offers a much more capable version of Siri that can answer questions conversationally, help with everyday tasks, and access personal information from a compatible iPhone or iPad. It can also recognize up to six members of a household, providing a personalized experience while keeping individual information private. However, some early owners have reported problems with Siri and other software features, as we explain below.
HomeView is designed to work alongside Apple’s existing HomePod speakers, Apple TV, iPhone, and iPad. It integrates with the Apple Home app, supporting compatible HomeKit and Matter accessories, including lights, locks, thermostats, and security cameras. It can also serve as a central smart-home hub, making it easier to manage devices and automations throughout the house.
Unlike a HomePod with a screen added, HomeView is designed around visual interaction as well as voice control. Its touchscreen, customizable widgets, FaceTime camera, personalized Home Screens, and dedicated smart-home dashboards make it more like a shared household computer than a conventional smart speaker. It comes in tabletop and wall-mounted versions, with prices starting at $299/£299.
What can Apple HomeView do?
HomeView introduces a range of capabilities that aren’t available on Apple’s traditional HomePod speakers. While HomePod focuses primarily on music, Siri, and voice-controlled smart-home functions, HomeView adds a touchscreen, camera, personalized interface, and much deeper integration with Apple apps and services.


FeatureWhat HomeView offers compared to HomePos

Smart-home dashboardTouchscreen controls for lights, locks, heating, scenes, and automations
Siri AIHomeView launches with Siri AI in beta, while HomePod mini 2’s support requires a later update. 
Siri Ai brings: natural conversations, broader knowledge, and personalized assistance with a compatible paired device
Personalized Home ScreenRecognizes up to six users by face and provides individual apps, widgets, and content
FaceTime video callsBuilt-in 12MP Center Stage camera for hands-free video calling
Calendar and remindersView appointments, manage tasks, set timers, and access personal information
Security camerasDisplay up to nine live camera feeds and access intelligent video descriptions
Music and videoView album artwork, lyrics, videos, and supported streaming content on the built-in display
Photos and customizable facesDisplay shared albums, photo collections, clocks, weather, and animated faces
Messages and communicationRead and respond to messages, make calls, and use Intercom
Recipes and household activitiesFollow step-by-step cooking instructions, manage timers, and access helpful information

 



HomeView also supports Handoff from iPhone, Live Activities, Find My, and multiroom audio with compatible AirPlay speakers.
How does HomeView compare with HomePod and iPad?
The biggest difference between HomeView and HomePod is the display. While a HomePod can control smart-home devices and play music using Siri, HomeView provides an interactive dashboard and visual feedback, making it more useful for managing a busy household.
HomeView also offers capabilities that make it a potential alternative to an iPad in certain situations. It can display recipes, calendars, photos, and video calls without needing someone to pick it up or unlock it. Its ability to recognize different household members and switch automatically between personalized experiences is particularly useful in a shared space.
However, HomeView isn’t intended to replace an iPad. The iPad remains the better choice for portable computing, productivity, games, and the broad selection of apps available from the App Store. HomeView is designed to stay in one place and provide convenient access to household information, entertainment, and smart-home controls.


Apple HomeView release date: When did it launch?
Announced: October 13, 2026 
Pre-orders: October 13, 2026 
In Store: November 13, 2026
Apple announced HomeView on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, as part of its “Welcome home” launch. Pre-orders opened the same day, with both the tabletop and wall-mounted models on sale from Friday, November 13.
HomeView is initially available in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, India, New Zealand, Singapore, and South Africa. Singapore pre-orders opened on October 15, while customers in South Africa can order through authorized resellers.
The device won’t initially be sold in the European Union because Siri AI isn’t currently available in iOS in the EU. Apple says it is working toward resolving the situation, but hasn’t announced a European release date.
HomeView can be ordered from the Apple website, Apple Store app, and selected retailers. It will also be displayed in Apple Stores. Apple hasn’t announced any general shipping delays beyond the roughly one-month gap between its announcement and retail availability, although individual delivery estimates may vary.
The November 13 date confirms the mid-November launch timeframe reported before the announcement. Earlier speculation about an October 30 launch is now superseded by Apple’s official schedule.

Apple HomeView design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			The HomeView from behind

Foundry




HomeView has a compact, square display mounted above a rounded aluminum speaker base, with a design that recalls Apple’s classic iMac G4. A stainless steel hinge allows the screen to tilt, making it easy to adjust the viewing angle when HomeView is positioned on a kitchen counter, desk, or bedside table.
The tabletop model is available in four colors: Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink, and Space Gray. The base incorporates the speakers, including a downward-firing woofer, while the display contains two additional full-range drivers. Apple uses 100 percent recycled aluminum in the base and includes a color-matched USB-C power cable.
The wall-mounted HomeView has a different design, with a slim square enclosure that’s just 0.39 inch thick. It is available in Silver and Space Gray and is designed for locations such as hallways and entrances. Unlike the tabletop model, it doesn’t include a separate woofer and requires a compatible wall mount, sold separately.
Both versions feature a touchscreen, built-in camera, four microphones, and USB-C power. Apple hasn’t listed conventional volume or power buttons in the published specifications, with touch and Siri providing the primary controls.

 The tabletop dimensions vary depending on the display’s tilt angle.






Does Apple HomeView have a camera?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Yes. Both HomeView models feature a built-in 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with an f/2.4 aperture.
The camera supports FaceTime video calling, with Center Stage automatically adjusting the framing to keep people visible as they move around or when additional participants join the conversation. Four beamforming microphones help pick up voices from across the room while reducing background noise.
The built-in camera cannot double as a security camera or provide an Echo Show-style video Drop In feature. HomeView can display feeds from compatible external security cameras, but that is a separate capability.
The camera also plays an important role in HomeView’s personalized features. It can recognize registered household members by face, automatically switching to their individual Home Screen and making their personal information available when the required security conditions are met.
Apple uses a protected processing environment called Secure Exclaves to isolate facial and voice recognition data from the operating system and apps. The system is designed so that the sensitive camera and microphone information used for recognition isn’t exposed to other users or Apple.
Apple hasn’t published more detailed video recording specifications, such as maximum capture resolution or frame rate.


						

							


What screen does Apple HomeView have?

				
					

				
			
HomeView

Foundry




HomeView features a 7-inch Liquid Retina touchscreen with a resolution of 1088 by 1088 pixels, giving it a pixel density of 220 pixels per inch. It uses an LED-backlit IPS panel with Multi-Touch support, True Tone, and a fingerprint-resistant oleophobic coating.
Maximum brightness reaches 500 nits, while minimum brightness drops to just 0.3 nits, making it suitable for a bedside table without lighting up the room at night.
The interface also adapts to proximity, showing simpler information when viewed from across the room and revealing more detail as someone approaches. Customizable faces include Photos, Calendar, Weather, Flow, and Snoopy.
The display is the same on the tabletop and wall-mounted models. Apple hasn’t specified a refresh rate, and there’s no OLED option.


						

							


HomeView audio: Speakers, Dolby Atmos and AirPlay
HomeView combines built-in speakers, Spatial Audio and AirPlay multiroom playback, with additional entertainment and personal features available through a paired iPhone or iPad.
Speakers and sound quality
Both models support Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos for music and video. Each has two full-range drivers in the display, while the tabletop model adds a down-firing woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators in its base. The wall-mounted version omits this speaker base, with Apple tuning its computational audio specifically for placement against a wall.
Our initial hands-on impressions placed the tabletop model between the HomePod mini and full-size HomePod for sound: it offered more weight and impact than the mini, while the larger HomePod delivered a bigger sound. These are early impressions; a full review will establish how both HomeView models perform.
Music, apps and multiroom playback
AirPlay lets HomeView join HomePod, HomePod mini and compatible speakers for music playback throughout your home. HomeView also supports FaceTime with Center Stage, Intercom broadcasts, and reading and replying to messages.
Compatible third-party audio and video apps run through your paired device, without requiring installation on HomeView. As our colleague Jason Cross explains, this uses a system based on CarPlay. Support depends on app compatibility, so check your preferred services before buying.
Siri AI and personal features
HomeView’s Siri AI supports conversational questions and music discovery without an Apple Intelligence-capable paired device. Personal-context requests, such as finding information in Messages or Calendar, require a paired Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad with Siri AI enabled in a supported language.
To display personal information, HomeView must recognize your face, and your paired device generally needs to be nearby and recently unlocked. This makes your iPhone or iPad an essential part of HomeView’s personalized experience. music throughout your home using HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini and compatible AirPlay speakers.


						

							


What processor does Apple HomeView use?
HomeView is powered by Apple’s A18 chip, the same generation of processor introduced with the iPhone 16 in 2024. This is considerably more powerful than the Apple Watch-derived processors used in older HomePod models and gives HomeView the processing capabilities needed for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.
The A18 is manufactured using a second-generation 3-nanometer process. In its original iPhone implementation, it features a six-core CPU, five-core GPU, and 16-core Neural Engine. Apple hasn’t confirmed whether the HomeView uses exactly the same CPU and GPU configuration, or whether the chip has been adapted for the new device.
The Neural Engine is particularly important because HomeView uses AI to support conversational Siri interactions, recognize household members, process camera and microphone information, and provide personalized responses. Apple’s Secure Exclaves also isolate sensitive recognition data from the operating system and applications.
Apple hasn’t revealed any performance comparisons between HomeView and previous HomePod processors, or disclosed any HomeView-specific improvements to chip packaging or manufacturing. However, the A18’s efficient 3nm architecture should help Apple deliver substantial processing power in a compact device that’s designed to operate continuously.
The A18 was one of the key specifications correctly predicted in our earlier HomeView rumors.


						

							




Apple HomeView connectivity and compatibility
HomeView supports Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 6.0, and Thread networking, giving it the wireless connectivity needed to communicate with Apple devices and compatible smart-home accessories.


ConnectivityHomeView specification

Wi-FiWi-Fi 6E (802.11ax) with MIMO
Wi-Fi bandsSimultaneous dual-band operation
BluetoothBluetooth 6.0
ThreadSupported

HomeKit / Apple HomeSupported

Ultra WidebandNot listed in Apple’s specifications
Cellular modemNo cellular connectivity announced
Satellite connectivityNot supported or advertised
Wired connectionUSB-C for power

 



HomeView integrates directly with Apple’s Home app and can control compatible smart lights, door locks, thermostats, blinds, and security cameras. It also supports Matter accessories, expanding compatibility beyond devices specifically designed for HomeKit.
Importantly, HomeView can act as a home hub itself. You don’t need to buy a separate HomePod or Apple TV simply to use HomeView as your smart-home hub. However, some advanced features depend on compatible accessories, an iCloud+ subscription, or an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. 
Apple has also announced the Apple Home Collection, a new lineup of cameras, thermostats, and a smart lock developed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. The first accessories will arrive in December 2026, with additional products following in early 2027.


Which iPhones and iPads work with HomeView?
Apple lists an iPhone running iOS 27.2 or later or an iPad running iPadOS 27.2 or later as a system requirement, alongside Wi-Fi internet access.
To use HomeView’s more personalized Siri AI features, you’ll need a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. Basic Siri AI functions, including general questions and conversational interactions, remain available without an Apple Intelligence-enabled companion device. Siri AI must be enabled on the paired device and set to a supported language, though.
HomeView also requires an Apple Account and compatible paired device for each household member who wants access to their personal information.


						

							


Does Apple HomeView have a battery or MagSafe charging?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Neither HomeView model has a built-in battery. Both are designed to remain connected to a power supply, so you can’t pick one up and use it around the house like an iPad.
The standard tabletop model includes a 1.5-meter USB-C cable and a 30W power adapter. Its USB-C connection supplies power rather than functioning as a conventional charging port.
The wall-mounted HomeView also requires continuous power, but Apple doesn’t include the wall mount, USB-C cable, or power adapter. These must be purchased separately, with a minimum 20W power adapter required when using a compatible USB-C power arrangement.
Apple offers three mounting solutions through Schneider Home, including a plug-in USB-C option, an AC-wired installation, and a Power over Ethernet (PoE) version coming in early 2027.


						

							


What software does Apple HomeView use?

				
					

				
			
Like a big Apple Watch

Apple




HomeView runs dedicated home-focused software built around Siri AI, Apple’s Home app, widgets, and a selection of familiar Apple applications. Apple identifies the initial Siri AI software as HomeView software version 27.2.
Rather than providing a conventional iPad interface, HomeView is designed to show useful information at a glance and respond to touch, voice, and proximity. Users can customize their Home Screen with apps and widgets, while special faces display photos, clocks, weather, calendar information, and animated artwork.
What can Siri AI do on HomeView?
Siri AI is one of HomeView’s biggest selling points. Powered by Apple Intelligence, it can answer open-ended questions, understand follow-up requests, draw on broad world knowledge, and support natural conversations.
For example, users can ask Siri to find a recipe, explain something they’re interested in, recommend music, control their smart-home accessories, or help organize everyday tasks.
When HomeView is paired with a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri becomes more personal. It can draw on information from Calendar, Messages, and other apps, helping users locate an invitation, check an appointment, or find relevant information without manually searching their devices.
Siri conversations can also continue across Apple devices using the Siri app, with conversation history privately synced through iCloud.
There are some limitations. Siri AI initially supports English, with Canadian French coming later. Certain AI features that use server-side models have daily usage limits, and Apple says expanded access will eventually be available for a fee. Siri AI launches in beta on HomeView software 27.2.


						

							




Which apps are available on HomeView?
Apple includes a selection of built-in apps and provides access to additional entertainment services through compatible iPhones.


Built-in appsAdditional apps and content

Calendar, Reminders, MessagesApple TV
FaceTime, Find My, IntercomApple News
Music, PodcastsAudiobooks
Home, SafariApple Music Classical
Weather, World ClockCompatible third-party audio and video apps
Alarms, Timers, SettingsSupported content and services from iPhone

 



HomeView supports third-party audio and video apps from compatible iPhones, but Apple hasn’t announced a dedicated HomeView App Store or general installation of iPad apps. That means it shouldn’t be regarded as a replacement for an iPad’s broader software capabilities.


How does HomeView work for different family members?
HomeView can recognize up to six users by their faces, automatically switching between personalized Home Screens and keeping each person’s content separate.
For example, one family member could approach HomeView and see their own calendar and reminders, while another would be shown different information. Shared photo albums, music, and general smart-home controls can still be enjoyed by everyone.
Access to personal information is more tightly controlled. The user’s paired iPhone or iPad must be on the same Wi-Fi network, must have been recently unlocked, and HomeView must recognize the person’s face.
Guests and unrecognized users can still ask Siri questions, play music, check the weather, set timers, and control eligible smart-home accessories, without gaining access to anyone’s private messages or calendars.


						

							


Is Apple HomeView secure?
Apple has designed HomeView with a particular emphasis on privacy, given that it includes an always-available camera and microphones in a shared household space. There is no physical camera/microphone privacy switch, but you can disable them via software controls.
The A18 chip uses Secure Exclaves to process camera and microphone data used for recognizing faces and voices. This information is isolated from the operating system and apps, so sensitive recognition data isn’t exposed to other software or Apple.
For Siri requests, HomeView can process information locally or use Private Cloud Compute, which Apple says handles cloud requests without storing the data or making it accessible to Apple.
HomeView also supports HomeKit Secure Video, including intelligent recognition of people, pets, packages, and vehicles with a compatible iCloud+ subscription. It can provide AI-generated descriptions of recorded activity, although these advanced features require setup with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.


						

							


How much does Apple HomeView cost?
Apple HomeView $299/£299
Apple HomeView (Wall Mounted) $299/£299
Apple HomeView starts at $299 in the U.S. and £299 in the U.K., with the tabletop and wall-mounted models carrying the same base price.
This positions HomeView below the $349 full-size HomePod price, although HomeView isn’t necessarily a direct replacement for that audio-focused speaker. 


						

							




Do HomeView wall mounts cost extra?
Yes. While the tabletop HomeView includes the accessories needed for power, the wall-mounted version requires additional purchases.


Schneider Home mounting accessoryU.S. priceAvailability

Power Mount USB-C Wall ConnectorFrom $59.95/£54.95Order now
Power Mount AC WiredFrom $79.95/£69.95Order now
Power Mount PoE Wired$129.95/£119.95Early 2027

 



For U.S. customers, this brings the minimum hardware cost of the wall-mounted HomeView and listed USB-C mount to $358.95/£353.95, before any additional installation or power accessories.


Is a larger HomeView coming?
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is developing a higher-end HomeView, codenamed J595, for a possible 2027 or 2028 release. It could feature a 9-inch display and a motorized arm offering 360-degree movement, allowing the screen to turn toward the speaker. Apple has not confirmed the product or its name; “Max” and “Ultra” are speculative. These rumored features are not part of the 7-inch HomeView that went on sale on November 13, 2026.


						

							


HomeView problems: What are owners reporting?
Some early HomeView owners have reported software problems, including Siri failing to respond, difficulty controlling music or setting timers, Photos errors, failed iPhone pairing during setup, and problems with automatic brightness and widgets retaining preferences.
Our November 16 report brings together complaints from MacRumors and Reddit. However, it is unclear how widespread the problems are or whether they share a common cause. Macworld’s Jason Cross has not encountered these issues during testing of the HomeView. 


						

							


Should you buy an Apple HomeView?
Apple HomeView looks particularly appealing for households already invested in Apple’s ecosystem. It brings together smart-home controls, a capable Siri assistant, video calling, entertainment, and personalized information in a single device that can be shared by everyone at home.
For families, its biggest advantage could be convenience. Being able to see calendars, reminders, weather, timers, and security cameras in a central location, while automatically switching between household members, makes HomeView more useful than a conventional smart speaker.
It’s also attractive for people with extensive HomeKit or Matter smart-home setups. Rather than relying on an iPhone whenever they want to adjust the heating, check a security camera, or activate a scene, users get a dedicated interface that’s always available.
However, HomeView won’t be essential for everyone. If you mainly use Siri to play music, set timers, and control a handful of smart lights, a HomePod mini is a considerably cheaper option. And if you already use an iPad on a stand in the kitchen, you may find that it handles many of the same tasks while offering much greater flexibility.
At $299/£299, HomeView is a premium alternative to smart displays from Amazon and Google. Its strongest selling points are its integration with Apple products, privacy-focused recognition of individual users, and the more powerful Siri AI experience. However, it’s worth remembering that some of those personalized AI features require a recent Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.
Given the early owner reports, we recommend waiting for fuller testing before buying specifically for Siri, music controls, or kitchen timers.


						

							


Which HomeView model should you buy?
For most people, the standard tabletop HomeView is the more sensible choice. It costs the same as the wallmounted version but includes a more substantial speaker system, an adjustable display, and the power accessories needed to get started.
The wallmounted version makes more sense if you want a permanent smarthome control panel in a hallway, entrance, or other shared area. Its slim design is more discreet, although the additional cost of mounting accessories and potentially professional installation makes it less affordable.
We’d recommend waiting for independent reviews before deciding whether HomeView’s sound quality, Siri performance, and personalized features justify its price. But for Apple households looking for a central smart-home display, HomeView already offers a combination of features that no existing HomePod can match.

title: iPhone 20 Pro Screen Protectors Show Rumored Curved Design
content:
Screen protector samples circulating online offer an early look at how Apple's rumored iPhone 20 Pro redesign could look, with rounded edges that could help create the appearance of a nearly borderless display.


Sharing a video of the purported screen protector on X yesterday, the leaker known as "Ice Universe" described next year's anticipated iPhone redesign as a "milestone." In a follow-up post on Weibo today, Ice Universe added, in translation, that "the era of easy screen protector application is coming to an end. The era of a comfortable grip is approaching."

The glass illustrates several elements repeatedly described in rumors about the anniversary iPhone, including shallow curves along all four edges, rounded corners, and an extremely narrow border.


The Apple iPhone 20 Pro is going to feature a milestone design - let's take a look first https://t.co/n8uNrZgh0S
— Ice Universe (@UniverseIce) November 16, 2026




October 7, Weibo blogger "体验more" shared photographs of samples in two sizes, suggesting that they looked like concept designs based on leaked information.

The screen protectors likely represent early manufacturing tests based on rumors, rather than parts made to Apple's actual specifications. Experimental pieces allow manufacturers to explore new manufacturing techniques ahead of having access to the finished device's dimensions.

Dynamic Island that appears comparable to the narrower version introduced on the iPhone 18 Pro. That would suggest no further substantial reduction for the anniversary model, in line with display analyst Ross Young's prediction that the smaller ‌Dynamic Island‌ would remain through 2027.

shallow curves alongside optical refraction and other visual effects to make the display borders less visible. 

That shape could also complicate screen protector designs. A protector covering the curved edges would need to follow their contours closely, making its fit dependent on the final glass geometry. Ice Universe's latest comments point to that potential tradeoff between a more rounded feel and the convenience of applying a flat protector.

glass similar to the iPhone Air, but with greater curvature on all four sides. Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected in the fall of 2027, although the "iPhone 20 Pro" name remains speculative.

title: iPhone, iPad targeted by massive website malware attack
content:
Visitors to over 170 major websites may have been affected by malicious code inserted through Optimizely trying to steal crypto and credit card data, with one vector of the attack focused on iPhones and iPads.


iPhones and iPads were targeted in a major web-based attack
While websites are frequently used as the attack vector to affect as many people as possible, it's rare for it to affect many major sites simultaneously. However, one part of the attack affecting the tool has potentially impacted iPhone users hanging on to older versions of iOS and iPadOS.
A flaw was found in Optimizely, a web experimentation platform for testing website elements, which enabled an attacker to place malicious JavaScript code. This code was then shown to users of websites that use the tool, potentially infecting viewers.

Apple released the entry-level M6 MacBook Pro in October, while the M5 Pro and M5 Max models got a higher-end option with a touchscreen PROLED XDR display and a lighter design at a $400 premium over the existing models. Compare its price with the newer model with the same screen size, memory, and storage. If the difference is small, consider whether the newer model’s improvements justify the extra cost. An older model with more memory or storage may be more useful to you than a newer model at a similar price.
Even with an M5 chip, the MacBook Air is still an excellent laptop for just about everyone. Amazon already dropped prices by $200-$250 in early November, which is the lowest we’ve seen since prices went up in June. We’ve seen prices for the 13-inch model with 512GB of storage drop as low as $1,099, so we’ll be on the lookout for it to drop under $1,000. Fingers crossed.

title: Longest-running Apple TV show to return for surprise 9th and 10th seasons
content:
Macworld





Slow Horses, one of the most consistently popular and successful shows to emerge from Apple’s TV streaming venture, has reportedly been renewed for a ninth and tenth season. This contradicts seemingly definitive comments from one of the show’s stars a few days ago indicating that it would conclude with the eighth season.
According to Deadline, Slow Horses “has been greenlighted by Apple TV for unprecedented ninth and 10th seasons.” It isn’t entirely clear where the site obtained this information, but there appears to be confirmation from Apple itself: Deadline adds that “an Apple spokeswoman said more is to come on synopses for Seasons 9 and 10.” We contacted Apple ourselves for a confirmation or denial, but the company didn’t immediately respond.
If accurate, this is surprising, because Olivia Cooke, a member of the main cast in the first season and a returning star in the most recent sixth, recently indicated (with the minor caveat of “never say never”) that it was drawing to a close. Speaking to The Times on November 14 while shooting the eighth season, Cooke went on record with the following surprisingly forthright remarks:
“I am shooting the last season!” she says. Is she supposed to say that? She laughs, then frowns. “Never say never!” she adds, backtracking. “But I think that’s what we’ve been told and it definitely feels like we are ending. We’re all melancholy, distracted. Yesterday, I got in the make-up chair and cried. The show’s been a shining light and I’ve told my partner I need two weeks to get over it. I’m going to be depressed.”
Aside from Cooke’s remarks, it seemed logical to expect a hiatus after the eighth season, at the very least, because the showrunners are running out of source material. The seventh and eighth seasons will be based on the Mick Herron novels Bad Actors and Clown Town, and he hasn’t written any more. Either he will need to get writing, or the show will need to go beyond his books.

PRICES CHECKED 17 NOVEMBER, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy an Apple Watch, with retailers discounting everything from the affordable SE to the premium Ultra. Last year’s U.S. offers included $50 off the SE 3, up to $70 off the then-new Series 11, and $100 off the Ultra 3. Older models brought bigger savings, including $150 off the Series 10 and $200 off the Ultra 2. In the U.K., clearance offers were particularly attractive: the Series 10 was up to £130 off at Currys, while Argos cut £200 from the Ultra 2’s original price.
October Prime Day brought discounts on this year’s models, too. In the U.S., the 42mm Series 12 fell to $349, the 40mm SE 3 to $199, and the Ultra 4 to $774 – savings of $50, $50, and $25 respectively. U.K. highlights included the SE 3 at £199 and the previous-generation Series 11 at £259.
This Black Friday, We’d look for discounts on the Series 12, our pick as the best Apple Watch for most people, the SE 3 for an affordable entry point, and the Ultra 4 for longer battery life and outdoor features. Remaining Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock could offer particularly good value if priced sufficiently below their replacements. Below, we explain which offers are worth taking and when to wait; for savings across Apple’s other products, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which Apple Watch should you buy this Black Friday?


Apple Watch Series 12 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			

Apple




The Series 12 is the Apple Watch we recommend for most people. It combines Apple’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate measurements, a Readiness score, and a tougher display with up to 24 hours of battery life.
A worthwhile Black Friday discount could make it an attractive purchase, but compare it with remaining Series 11 stock. The older model has the same quoted battery life, so a substantial saving may outweigh the newer health features.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has already discounted the 42mm GPS Series 12 to $329, a savings of $70 and the best price we’ve ever seen. The 46mm version is also $70 off.
U.K. Black Friday price: We didn’t see Series 12 discounts during October Prime Day and so far this November there have been no price drops, but we are hopeful. We have only seen discounts on older models so far.


						

							


Apple Watch Ultra 4 – Best for battery life and outdoor adventures

				
					

				
			

Apple




The Ultra 4 is our choice for endurance athletes, outdoor enthusiasts, and buyers who prioritize battery life. It offers up to 50 hours of normal use, satellite communication, precision dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and Apple’s new Health Sensing System.
It’s more watch than most people need, but the current $699.99 offer is substantially below October Prime Day’s $774 price, making it worth considering if you want the latest Ultra. Compare it with the Ultra 3, though, which retains many of its outdoor features but has a shorter 42-hour battery-life rating.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the Ultra 4 down to $774, a $25 saving. This November we’ve already seen the Apple Watch Ultra 4 for $699.99 on Amazon: that’s $99 off. 
U.K. Black Friday price: The Ultra 4 remained at its full £749 price during October Prime Day, but we’ve already seen it drop by £30 to £719 at Amazon.


						

							


Apple Watch SE 3 – Our best budget choice

				
					

				
			
Apple / Amazon




The SE 3 is the best-value option for buyers who want the core Apple Watch experience. It includes an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging, and the S10 chip, but lacks ECG, blood oxygen monitoring, and the newer Health Sensing System.
It remains part of Apple’s current lineup despite launching in 2025. A strong Black Friday offer could make it an excellent affordable purchase, although its previous discounts mean there’s little reason to settle for a token reduction.
U.S. Black Friday price: Both last Black Friday and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to $199 and the 44mm version to $229 – $50 below their regular prices. Already, the U.S. price is $199, $50 off at Amazon.
U.K. Black Friday price: Black Friday 2025 and October Prime Day brought the 40mm GPS model to £199 and the 44mm version to £229, saving £20. So far we haven’t seen any price drops for Black Friday 2026.


						

							


Apple Watch Ultra 3 – Best clearance option for outdoor enthusiasts

				
					

				
			
Apple




The Ultra 3 is worth considering if you want a rugged Apple Watch without paying for the latest model. It offers satellite communication, dual-frequency GPS, diving features, and up to 42 hours of battery life.
You give up the Ultra 4’s longer battery life and newer Health Sensing System. Compare their actual selling prices: the Ultra 3 needs to be sufficiently cheaper to justify choosing the older generation.
U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the Ultra 3 fell to $699, a $100 saving. Our October Prime Day coverage found only used models, so it didn’t identify a comparable new-stock offer. So far this November we’ve seen the Apple Watch Ultra 3 for $649, but that’s out of stock now.

Apple Watch Series 11 – Best clearance option for everyday use

				
					

				
			
Apple Watch Series 11




The Series 11 could be a better-value everyday watch than the Series 12 if the price gap is large enough. It has the same quoted 24-hour battery life, although it lacks the newer Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features.
For buyers who don’t need those additions, a substantial clearance discount could be more useful than a small saving on the latest model.
U.S. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the 42mm GPS Series 11 reached $339, while the 46mm version was $359 – savings of $60 and $70, respectively. Our October Prime Day coverage found only used models in the U.S. and so far that’s all we are seeing this November.

Should you buy an Apple Watch now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need an Apple Watch immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer matches or comes close to a previous low for the same model and configuration, it can be worth taking – particularly if you want a specific size, color, or band combination.
October Prime Day prices provide useful benchmarks. In the U.S., the Series 12 fell to $349 for the 42mm GPS model and $399 for the 46mm version, while the Ultra 4 reached $774. The SE 3 was $199 in 40mm and $229 in 44mm. Those SE prices also appeared last Black Friday, so we’d look for offers matching or beating them. In the U.K., October highlights included the 40mm SE 3 at £199 and the older 42mm Series 11 at £259.
The Series 12 and Ultra 4 only arrived in September, so finding a better price is the main reason to wait. If you don’t need a watch immediately, those previous offers give you a useful starting point for deciding whether to buy now or hold out.
Compare retailers, too. Last Black Friday, Walmart offered $150 off the Series 10, while U.K. shoppers could find up to £130 off at Currys and £200 off the Ultra 2’s original price at Argos. Our guide to the best time to buy an Apple Watch has more advice on choosing when to purchase.


						

							


Should you buy an older Apple Watch?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t assume an older Apple Watch is a bad buy. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are only one generation old and can make excellent purchases if they’re substantially cheaper than the Series 12 or Ultra 4. Both retain many of their replacements’ core features, although you miss the newer Health Sensing System and, with the Ultra 3, the Ultra 4’s longer battery life.
Compare actual selling prices, matching case size, material, connectivity, and band where possible. A $50 difference between a Series 11 and Series 12 may not be enough to justify giving up the newer model’s health features, whereas a substantially larger saving could change the calculation. A discounted Series 11 could also be worth considering alongside the SE 3 if a small premium gets you features you’ll use.
Be much more cautious with the Series 8, SE 2, and original Ultra: those models cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 9 is the oldest standard Apple Watch compatible with the latest software, while the Ultra 2 is the oldest supported Ultra and the SE 3 is the only supported SE. Missing the latest software doesn’t make an older watch unusable, but it makes it harder to recommend as a purchase today.
The Series 9, Series 10, and Ultra 2 can still be worth considering at sufficiently low prices. However, compatibility with today’s software doesn’t guarantee how many future upgrades they’ll receive. Weigh the savings against the watch’s age and features, rather than assuming every supported generation offers equally good value.


						

							


Apple Watch deals to avoid 

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t let a bigger advertised discount tempt you into paying more for a cellular Apple Watch you won’t use. If your iPhone is usually nearby, a GPS model can already handle calls, messages, and notifications through your phone. It can also track runs, use Apple Pay, and play downloaded music without your iPhone. As our experience testing a cellular Apple Watch showed, the extra connectivity may add little to everyday use.
Cellular is worth considering if you regularly leave your iPhone behind and want to remain contactable without Wi-Fi, or you’re setting up a watch for a child without an iPhone. Otherwise, you could pay extra for the hardware and then add an ongoing mobile-plan charge for a feature you rarely need. You don’t have to activate a plan on a cellular model, so it can still be a good buy if its sale price matches or beats the GPS version. Our GPS versus cellular Apple Watch guide explains the trade-offs.
Check the rest of the configuration, too. A premium case material or expensive band can make a heavily discounted watch cost more than a simpler version that meets your needs. Judge offers against previous selling prices as well as the advertised reduction: a large saving from the original launch price doesn’t necessarily mean exceptional value. Check any spending requirements, contracts, trade-ins, or rebates attached to offers advertising a “free” Apple Watch.
Finally, check whether you’re buying a new, refurbished, or used watch, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For a used or refurbished model, check the stated battery condition and confirm that it has been removed from the previous owner’s account, with Activation Lock turned off. Make sure the watch is compatible with your iPhone before ordering.


						

							


How we choose Apple Watch deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on Apple Watch reviews and everyday wear. We consider comfort, performance, battery life, charging, health and fitness features, and value – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our Series 12 review assessed battery life and charging performance alongside its newer health features. We also draw on everyday experience: our cellular Apple Watch testing examines whether staying connected without an iPhone justified the extra hardware and subscription costs.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. We check the generation, case size, material, connectivity, and included band so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside discounted replacements.
Our Best Apple Watch guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the right choice: your budget, wrist size, activities, and the features you need all matter.

title: Chip shortage forces Apple to sign long-term contract with Samsung
content:
Apple is reportedly close to securing supplies of DRAM for the iPhone for the next several years, but on terms that appear unusually favorable for supplier Samsung.


Apple is having to commit to longer-term contracts for memory supplies - image credit: Apple.
Apple had managed to ride out the global chip shortage for some time because of existing orders. However, by February 2026, it was reportedly having to agree to pay double its previous amount for DRAM.
That deal was with Samsung and appears to have been for some or all of 2026. Now according to Korean news site Maeil Business Newspaper, Samsung is at least close to securing a deal that should see it supplying DRAM to Apple until 2031 or 2032.

title: iPhone Users Targeted in Major Website Security Breach
content:
Hackers used some of the world's most popular websites to distribute malware designed to steal cryptocurrency and exploit vulnerabilities in iPhones and iPads this week, according to a new security investigation.


Reuters reports that websites associated with 178 organizations were affected by the attack on Monday, November 16, including the likes of Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, and IKEA.

Optimizely, a third-party platform that companies use to test and customize their websites. Hackers managed to insert malicious JavaScript into Optimizely's customer projects, allowing them to distribute the malware through legitimate websites without directly compromising their infrastructure.

discovered the attack. Helme found that the malicious scripts could replace legitimate cryptocurrency wallet addresses with ones controlled by the attackers, as well as intercept payment card details, steal browser cookies, and take screenshots.

The code was especially targeted at iPhone and iPad users. Visitors could be served one of two exploit kits – Coruna and DarkSword – through a hidden webpage element, depending on their device's software version. Coruna reportedly targeted devices running iOS 13 through iOS 17, while DarkSword targeted iOS 18. Researchers also found code targeting iOS 26, but this appeared to be limited to identifying devices' characteristics.

The attack potentially allowed malicious code to execute simply by visiting an affected website – users did not need to download an app or interact with a suspicious link. That said, it's still unclear whether any iPhones or iPads were successfully compromised.

BleepingComputer that attackers managed to exploit a vulnerability in its account signup process, causing websites using the platform to load malware. The flaw has since been patched, the malicious code has been removed, and affected customers have been notified, according to the company.

title: Best AirPods Black Friday deals 2026: Our picks for Pro, standard AirPods and Max
content:

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 17 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy AirPods, with retailers competing to offer discounts across Apple’s earbuds and over-ear headphones. Previous sales have brought substantial savings on established models, clearance bargains on older generations, and even discounts on newly released AirPods. But the biggest percentage saving doesn’t necessarily mean the best buy: an older pair needs to be sufficiently cheaper than its replacement to justify missing out on newer features.
Last Black Friday, standard AirPods 4 briefly dropped to $69 in the U.S., while the noise-canceling version fell to $99 – an $80 saving. Even the then-new AirPods Pro 3 received a discount of around $30, while older AirPods Pro 2 reached approximately $139 before selling out. AirPods Max were available for around $400, roughly $150 below their regular price. U.K. savings were more modest, with AirPods 4 at £99 and AirPods Pro 2 at £169, although stock frequently ran out.
This year, we’d watch AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2 for meaningful discounts, while remaining AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 stock could bring some of the biggest clearance savings. The recently released AirPods 5 may see smaller reductions, making it especially important to compare their price with discounted Pro models. Below, we explain which AirPods to choose and how the offers compare with previous discounts. For savings on Macs, iPads, Apple Watch and more, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which AirPods should you buy this Black Friday?


AirPods Pro 3 – Our best overall choice

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Pro 3 are especially worth considering if you want strong noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit, or Apple’s hearing-health features. Their foam-infused ear tips help improve the fit, while an in-ear heart-rate sensor adds another reason to choose them over standard AirPods. Battery life is rated at up to eight hours with noise cancellation enabled.
For most buyers looking for noise-isolating earbuds, these would be our first choice. Older AirPods Pro 2 are worth considering only when the clearance savings are substantial.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has already slashed almost $70 off the AirPods Pro 3, but we expect the price to go lower. Hopefully, by Black Friday, they will hit their all-time low of $169.
U.K. Black Friday price: Earlier in November, AirPods Pro 3 were £30 off in the U.K. They now cost £200, a saving of £19.


						

							


AirPods 5 – Best for buyers who prefer earbuds without silicone tips

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 5 offer a lower-cost entry point and an open-ear design for people who don’t like silicone-tipped earbuds. They include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, alongside Transparency mode and Adaptive Audio.
Check which charging case you’re buying. The Wireless Charging Case package adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker, and volume adjustment by swiping the stems. It’s our preferred package when the price difference is small.
U.S. Black Friday price: We’ve not seen a discount yet on the AirPods 5.
U.K. Black Friday price:  No savings yet on the AirPods 5.


						

							


AirPods Max 2 – Best for over-ear listening

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods Max 2 are the option to consider if you specifically want over-ear headphones. The March 2026 update introduced Apple’s H2 chip and improved noise cancellation, while retaining the premium design and a choice of colors.
We find them difficult to recommend at full price, so the size of the discount matters. Compare any offer with previous sale prices rather than judging it solely against Apple’s asking price.
U.S. Black Friday price:  Amazon has the AirPods Max 2 for $449, that’s $99 off. They could still go lower though.
U.K. Black Friday price:  The AirPods Max 2 are £449 at Amazon – that’s £50 off. You can get the same deal at AO and Boots. 


						

							


Other AirPods – Buy only at a worthwhile clearance price

				
					

				
			
Apple




AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 can still be worth considering, but compare them with the discounted prices of their replacements. A large reduction from an older model’s launch price can disguise a small saving over a newer, more capable pair.
Check the exact generation, charging case, condition, and seller before buying. For more help choosing, read our AirPods buying guide.
U.S. Black Friday price:  There’s $122 off the former price of the AirPods Pro 2 at Walmart, meaning you can grab a pair for just $127.
U.K. Black Friday price:  You can get the AirPods 4 with ANC for £109 at John Lewis – but that’s only £10 less than AirPods 5, so we’d recommend waiting for that price to go even lower.


						

							


Other headphones – Worthy AirPods alternatives

				
					

				
			
Beats




If AirPods aren’t in your budget, Apple also sells a line of Beats headphones and earbuds that offer many of the same features for a lower price, including the popular on-ear Solo 4 and Powerbeats Pro 2. We’ll also track headphone deals in our roundup of the best earbuds for iPhone and best over-ear headphones if you’d like to see deals on other brands.
U.S. Black Friday price:  There is $100 off the Beats Studio Pro and $70 off the Solo 4 at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.
U.K. Black Friday price:  There is £64 off the Powerbeats Pro 2 and £50 off the Powerbeats Fit at Amazon, but we expect to see more discounts later in November.

Should you buy AirPods now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need AirPods immediately. But the sales now stretch across much of November, so you don’t necessarily need to wait for Black Friday itself. If an early offer is close to a model’s previous low, it can be worth taking: last year’s best deals frequently sold out, and popular offers could go quickly again.
Previous sale prices provide useful benchmarks. We’ve seen AirPods Pro 3 reach $169, while AirPods Max 2 fell to $399 during June Prime Day. An offer above those prices may still be worth considering, but a reduction from Apple’s regular price doesn’t automatically make it an exceptional deal.
For AirPods 5, waiting for a discount makes sense if you aren’t in a hurry: they didn’t receive a significant reduction during October Prime Day. With AirPods Max 2, we’d hold out for a substantial saving rather than pay full price.
Compare retailers, too. Amazon isn’t always cheapest: Walmart and Best Buy also compete on AirPods pricing, while Argos offered competitive U.K. deals last year. Our guide to the best time to buy AirPods has more advice on purchase timing.


						

							


Should you buy an old pair of AirPods? 
Older-generation AirPods can be a good buy at the right clearance price. Compare their actual selling price with the discounted price of their replacement, rather than focusing on the percentage saving from an old launch price. A substantial discount can make an older pair worthwhile; a small difference may leave you sacrificing useful features for little saving.
AirPods 4 are harder to recommend now that AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, starting at the same $129 price previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC. Check which AirPods 4 version you’re buying—there were models with and without noise cancellation—and look for a substantial saving over AirPods 5.
AirPods Pro 2 remain worth considering if they’re significantly cheaper than Pro 3. However, the newer model improves fit, noise cancellation, and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing. Compare their sale prices carefully: a strong Pro 3 discount could make the older pair’s clearance offer less attractive.
The original AirPods Max also need a substantial discount to justify choosing them over Max 2. The newer headphones add the H2 chip, improved noise cancellation, and features including Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. Check the generation rather than relying on the charging port alone: the original AirPods Max were also sold in a USB-C version.
Buying older stock new is different from buying used or refurbished AirPods. For those pairs, check the stated condition, charging case, warranty, and returns policy, and buy from a reputable seller. Be cautious about battery condition and unusually low marketplace prices, since convincing counterfeits can resemble genuine AirPods. Our guide explains how to spot fake AirPods.
For more advice, see our AirPods buying guide and guide to the best time to buy AirPods.


						

							


AirPods deals to avoid

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Check exactly what an offer includes before comparing prices. Different charging-case packages can affect features and value, so make sure you’re comparing equivalent versions. Also check any spending requirements, contracts, or rebates attached to offers advertising “free” AirPods.
Judge the price against previous selling prices as well as the advertised discount. A large saving from the recommended retail price doesn’t necessarily mean a particularly good deal if retailers regularly charge less.
Check whether the listing is for a new, refurbished, or used pair. For used or refurbished AirPods, look for clear information about condition, warranty, and returns coverage. Battery condition deserves particular caution: a low purchase price may be less attractive if listening time has deteriorated.
Finally, check who is selling and dispatching your order, particularly when shopping through a marketplace. Unusually low prices from unfamiliar sellers warrant caution, since counterfeit AirPods can look convincing. Our guide explains how to tell if AirPods are fake.


						

							


How we choose AirPods deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on AirPods reviews. We consider sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, battery life, and everyday use – not just the specifications or advertised saving.
Our testing helps us explain which features are worth paying for. For example, our AirPods Pro 3 review assessed how securely the redesigned ear tips stayed in place during exercise, checked battery life against Apple’s claims, and evaluated the heart-rate sensor. Our AirPods Max 2 review weighed their excellent sound and noise cancellation against drawbacks including weight and the Smart Case.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous lows to judge whether an offer represents good value. Our Best AirPods guide explains why the most expensive model isn’t necessarily the best choice for everyone: fit, listening habits, and the features you need all matter.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best Mac deals, iPad deals, and Apple Watch deals.
