PRICES CHECKED 17 NOVEMBER 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is a great time to buy an iPad, with discounts spanning affordable everyday tablets, powerful Pro models, and clearance stock from previous generations. Last year’s U.S. offers included $150 off the M3 iPad Air, $100 off the A17 Pro iPad mini, and $100 off the then-new M5 iPad Pro. The standard A16 iPad has previously reached $271. In the U.K., highlights included £100 off the iPad Air, £50 off the mini, and substantial savings on older M4 iPad Pro models.
October Prime Day brought further discounts, although Apple’s June price increases made the advertised savings less straightforward. In the U.S., the 128GB A16 iPad was $399, the 128GB A17 Pro mini was $499, and the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB was $649. U.K. offers included £80 off the 13-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB. Those prices show why it’s worth checking previous selling prices as well as today’s discount: an offer below Apple’s current asking price may still cost more than the same iPad did earlier in the year.
This Black Friday, we’d watch the M4 iPad Air for a balance of performance and price, the A16 iPad for a worthwhile budget deal, and the M5 iPad Pro for buyers who need its premium capabilities. The new A20 Pro iPad mini, with its OLED display, also changes the calculation: we’d expect smaller initial discounts on the new arrival, while remaining A17 Pro stock could offer clearance bargains. Below, we explain which deals are worth taking, checking the generation, storage, and connectivity rather than simply choosing the biggest advertised saving. For offers across Apple’s other products, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which iPad should you buy this Black Friday?


M4 iPad Air – Our best all-round choice

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Air offers a strong balance of performance, screen size, and price without the premium cost of the Pro. The 11-inch model suits buyers who prioritize portability, while the 13-inch version gives you more room for multitasking and creative work.
A good Black Friday discount could make either size an attractive purchase. Compare storage capacities carefully, though: a larger advertised saving on a high-capacity model isn’t necessarily better value if you don’t need the extra space.
U.S. Black Friday price: At Amazon, you can already get a saving of $100 off some iPad Air models. Last Black Friday, the 11-inch and 13-inch M3 models were $449 and $649, respectively, which was $150 off the old price, so we hope to see discounts of at least $150 again, although starting prices are now considerably higher.
U.K. Black Friday price: There’s £49 off the 128GB 13-inch iPad Air and £44 off the 256GB 11-inch iPad Air. These are reasonable savings, although we saw better discounts during October Prime Day, with up to £144 off. Last Black Friday, selected M3 Air configurations received £100 discounts.


						

							


iPad Pro – Best for demanding creative work

				
					

				
			
Apple Inc




The iPad Pro is the option for buyers who need Apple’s highest-end tablet performance and premium display. It comes in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes, but its capabilities – and price – will exceed what many people need for browsing, streaming, and everyday apps.
We’d look for a substantial saving rather than buy simply because it’s the most powerful iPad. Compare discounted M4 iPad Pro models, too: an older Pro could offer better value if its price is sufficiently below the equivalent M5 configuration.
U.S. Black Friday price:  During October Prime Day, the 11-inch M5 Pro with 256GB was $1,099, saving $100. So far we’re seeing nearly $300 off a 1TB 11-inch iPad Pro.
U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought little to recommend on the M5 Pro, with reductions of around £12. Last Black Friday, older M4 iPad Pro offers included a saving of approximately £206 at Amazon. Currently, the biggest saving is £150 off the 11-inch, 1TB model.


						

							


iPad (A16) – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Apple




The A16 iPad remains a capable option for browsing, streaming, schoolwork, and everyday use. However, Apple raised its starting price by $100/£100 in June, and it doesn’t support Apple Intelligence.
That makes the final purchase price particularly important. A modest discount from today’s higher asking price may still leave you paying more than this iPad previously cost. With a replacement expected early in 2027, we’d look for a substantial Black Friday saving and compare the price with discounted iPad Air models before buying.
U.S. Black Friday price: The 128GB A16 iPad was $399 during October Prime Day, saving $50 against its increased $449 price. Last Black Friday, it briefly reached $279. This Black Friday we are already seeing $49 off the 128GB iPad. However, at $399.99, this isn’t an offer we’d rush to buy. It approximately matches October’s $399 price and is well above the $279 we saw last Black Friday. We’d wait for a better discount as Black Friday approaches.
U.K. Black Friday price: October coverage listed the 256GB model at £499.97, around £29 off. Last Black Friday, the 128GB version was £299 and the 256GB version was £399. We hope to see even lower prices this year, but so far the discount is £30 off the iPad.


						

							


iPad mini with A20 Pro – Best for portability

				
					

				
			
Apple




The new iPad mini went on sale on November 6, replacing the A17 Pro model. It brings an 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, and a thinner, lighter design, making it the option to consider if you want a compact iPad with the latest hardware.
Because it has only just arrived, we’d expect initial discounts to be smaller than clearance savings on its predecessor. The older A17 Pro mini could still be worthwhile at a sufficiently low price, but compare the saving with what you give up – particularly the new display.
U.S. Black Friday price: The A20 Pro mini wasn’t available during October Prime Day or last Black Friday. Its 128GB A17 Pro predecessor was $499 during October Prime Day and $399 last Black Friday. Unsurprisingly, there are no discounts on the new models – but you can save around $200 on the price of the A17 Pro iPad mini compared to the newer equivalent. This is the same offer we saw during October Prime Day.
U.K. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought only a small saving on the A17 Pro mini in our coverage. The 128GB version reached £399 earlier this year, though – before Apple pushed up prices. You can still get the A17 Pro iPad mini for £100 less than the new model, but we hope to see bigger savings as Black Friday approaches.

Should you buy an iPad now or wait for a better deal?

				
					

				
			
There’s an iPad for everyone.

Foundry




With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need an iPad immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if the price is competitive. Compare the exact generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity rather than waiting for Black Friday simply because a larger discount might appear.
Previous selling prices are particularly important this year because Apple raised iPad prices in June. During October Prime Day, the 128GB A16 iPad was $399, while the 11-inch M4 iPad Air with 128GB was $649. Both were discounted against Apple’s increased prices, but cost more than their regular prices before June. A saving from today’s asking price doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting an exceptional bargain.
For the M4 iPad Air and M5 iPad Pro, we’d focus on finding a good price: We don’t expect replacements until 2027, as explained in our guide to the best time to buy an iPad. We’d be more cautious about the A16 iPad, which lacks Apple Intelligence and is expected to be replaced. Unless you find a substantial saving, waiting could get you a more capable entry-level model.
The new A20 Pro iPad mini presents a different decision. It has only just arrived, so we’d expect smaller initial discounts rather than immediate clearance-level savings. If you want its OLED display and newer processor, a modest reduction may still be worthwhile. If price matters more, compare remaining A17 Pro stock – but make sure the saving justifies choosing the older hardware.


						

							


Should you buy an older iPad? 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older iPad can be a good buy if its price reflects its age and the features you give up. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of its replacement, matching screen size, storage, and connectivity where possible. A large saving from an old launch price doesn’t necessarily make it better value.
The M3 iPad Air and M4 iPad Pro are worth considering at substantial clearance discounts. Both remain capable options, and you may get more benefit from a lower price or additional storage than from the latest processor. However, if the newer equivalent costs only slightly more, the saving may not justify choosing the older generation.
The A17 Pro iPad mini also deserves consideration now that the A20 Pro model has arrived. It supports Apple Intelligence and remains a capable compact tablet, but you miss the newer model’s OLED display, faster processor, and thinner, lighter design. We’d want a meaningful saving rather than a small reduction from its former asking price.
Be more cautious with much older models. Check whether they support the current version of iPadOS and the apps and features you need. Compatibility today doesn’t guarantee how many future software upgrades they’ll receive. Apple Intelligence support also varies: don’t assume every older Air, Pro, or mini includes it.
If you already own an Apple Pencil or keyboard, check compatibility before changing generations. Keeping compatible accessories could make an older iPad better value, while replacing them could erase part of your saving. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges.


						

							


iPad deals to avoid
Check the exact configuration before comparing offers. Retailer listings can emphasize iPad, Air, or Pro without making the generation obvious. Confirm the chip, screen size, storage capacity, and whether you’re buying Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi + Cellular. A cheaper listing may be a different model rather than a better deal.
Don’t let a large advertised discount tempt you into paying for storage or connectivity you won’t use. A heavily reduced high-capacity or cellular iPad can still cost more than a simpler configuration that meets your needs. Compare the final purchase prices, rather than assuming the biggest saving represents the best value.
Check whether the price includes nano-texture glass, too. This optional finish reduces glare and makes fingerprints and oily smudges less noticeable, which can be useful if reflections make your iPad difficult to see in bright rooms or outdoors. It avoids much of the washed-out appearance associated with ordinary matte finishes, but contrast can drop at some viewing angles and the surface may be more scratch-sensitive. Availability depends on the model and storage configuration, so you could end up paying for both the finish and additional storage. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may be better value. Read our guide to nano-texture glass and whether you need it.
Our iPad buying guide considers cellular a luxury for most buyers. If you mainly use your iPad somewhere with Wi-Fi, you may get little benefit from the extra hardware. For occasional use elsewhere, sharing your iPhone’s connection through Personal Hotspot can be a more economical option.
Cellular makes more sense if you regularly need an independent connection while commuting or traveling; it also adds built-in GPS for accurate location tracking. Factor in any data-plan charges and compare the total cost of a contract with buying outright. A cellular model can still be worthwhile if its sale price matches or beats the equivalent Wi-Fi version—you don’t have to activate a data plan simply because the hardware is included.
Judge savings against previous selling prices as well as Apple’s current price. Following June’s price increases, a discounted iPad may still cost more than it did earlier in the year. Also distinguish a cash discount from a gift-card offer: a gift card doesn’t reduce the amount you pay for the iPad and is useful only if you’ll spend it.
Check what any bundle includes. A keyboard, case, or stylus doesn’t automatically make an offer better value, particularly if the accessories aren’t the versions you want. Read the conditions attached to “free” iPads, trade-in promotions, contracts, and rebates before comparing their total cost with buying outright.
Finally, check whether the iPad is new, refurbished, or used, who is selling it, and what warranty and returns policy apply. For used or refurbished models, look for information about battery condition and confirm that Activation Lock has been removed. Be cautious about devices that remain tied to a previous owner or an organization’s management system.


						

							


How we choose iPad deals
Macworld’s editors have decades of experience with Apple devices, and our recommendations draw on hands-on iPad reviews and everyday use. We consider performance, display quality, portability, battery life, and accessory support alongside price to explain which iPads suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess whether paying more brings practical benefits. A faster processor or premium display may matter for demanding creative work, while a less expensive iPad can be perfectly capable of browsing, streaming, and schoolwork. We also consider the cost of keyboards, Apple Pencils, and other accessories when judging an iPad’s value.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the generation, screen size, storage, and connectivity so that comparisons reflect what you’re actually buying. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than relying solely on savings against today’s recommended price.
Older models can be worthwhile clearance purchases, but only when their prices make sense alongside newer alternatives. Our iPad buying guide explains the differences between the ranges, while our purchase-timing guide helps you decide whether to buy now or wait.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best Mac deals, AirPods deals, and Apple Watch deals.

title: Apple, please bring that new iPhone Duo feature to my MacBook
content:
Macworld





With the iOS 27.3 beta 2 that was released on Monday, Apple unveiled a cool new feature for iPhone Duo users. I don’t own a Duo, but it’s such a cool feature I’m really hoping Apple brings it to the MacBook.
One of the iPhone Duo’s biggest flaws is that the front camera doesn’t have Face ID and instead relies on Touch ID for unlocking. But in the iOS 27.3 beta 2, Apple provided a surprisingly clever workaround. The front camera will be able to be used to unlock the iPhone Duo if the phone had performed a Touch ID or password authentication in the past 45 minutes. It’s not true Face ID, but it’s a handy workaroud that considers both security and convenience.
Essentially, Apple ported HomeView’s new facial recognition method over to the iPhone Duo. It’s not as secure as Face ID and can’t be used for purchases or login authentication, but it makes it so much easier to quickly unlock your phone to see notifications or send a quick text. 
So now that Apple has a facial unlock devices with the front camera, how about bringing this feature over to the Mac? Since this new unlock method doesn’t require the Face ID module, it could work on existing MacBook Pro models. Since Apple didn’t add a TrueDepth camera to the new MacBook Pro, full Face ID is likely a long ways off, if it ever happens. But now Apple has shown that it can be done without upgrading the front camera.
Touch ID works great, but it’s not the most efficient way to authenticate. I’ve wanted Face ID on the MacBook for as long as I can remember, and even if it only works for unlocking, this implementation sounds like a more than acceptable compromise. Here’s hoping it shows up in a future macOS beta.

title: Apple Tests Bringing Back a Softer Side of Liquid Glass
content:
Apple is testing a softer appearance for iPhone navigation bars that would bring back part of the look used in iOS 26, according to a new finding shared by pdfu on X (Twitter).

The gradual fade nav bar effect is disabled by default in iOS 27.3 beta 2

The change affects how content fades out as it scrolls beneath the bar at the top of an app, so that text and other elements disappear into a gentler blur, rather than meeting a more sharply defined boundary.

In the side-by-side comparison above, shared by pdfu, the difference is shown with the test feature switched off – the navigation bar has a distinct lower edge separating it from the list below. With the feature enabled (as shown on the right), the boundary is replaced by a softer, more gradual transition.

According to pdfu, the effect is designed to appear when Liquid Glass tint is set to 25 percent or lower, and it only applies to navigation bars that use the default style. The gentler fade is currently disabled behind an internal feature flag in the latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, so it's not at a stage where users can simply turn on the change via Settings.

reworked Liquid Glass in iOS 27 with changes aimed at improving readability, including a more uniform background behind content at the top of apps. It also replaced the earlier Clear and Tinted presets with a continuous transparency slider, offering users finer control over the Liquid Glass appearance.

PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 17, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
Black Friday is one of the best opportunities to save on a Mac, with retailers competing to discount MacBooks and desktop models – including recently released machines. Last year, U.S. shoppers could get a 13-inch M4 MacBook Air for $749, saving $250, while the then-new 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro fell to $1,349, also $250 off. Selected M4 Max MacBook Pro configurations received $500 discounts. U.K. highlights included £150 off the entry-level M4 MacBook Air and savings of around £350 on selected MacBook Pro models.
This year’s deals need a different perspective because Apple raised Mac prices in June. The MacBook Air went up by $200/£200, while some MacBook Pro configurations increased by as much as $500/£500. October Prime Day helped offset those increases: the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB storage fell to $1,099, saving $200, while selected high-end MacBook Pros received discounts of up to $600. Desktop offers included around $120 off the entry-level M6 Mac mini and $200 off the M5 Max Mac Studio.
Those increases mean we may not see a return to earlier record-low prices this Black Friday, even when retailers offer substantial discounts. However, November’s sales could still bring some of the best prices available under Apple’s higher pricing, making this a worthwhile time to buy if you need a new Mac. We’re comparing current offers with previous selling prices and equivalent configurations – not simply the biggest advertised saving – to help you identify genuine value. Below, you’ll find our picks across MacBooks and desktop Macs; for discounts on Apple’s other products, see our best Apple Black Friday deals.
Which Mac or MacBook should you buy this Black Friday?


MacBook Air – Our best overall choice 

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The MacBook Air is our recommendation for most buyers. Both sizes offer a lightweight, silent laptop for everyday work, studying, and occasional creative projects. Choose the 13-inch for portability or the 15-inch for more workspace without MacBook Pro pricing.
We’d prioritize a competitive price on the memory and storage you need. For regular lengthy exports or other sustained demanding tasks, consider a MacBook Pro with active cooling instead.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 13-inch M5 Air with 16GB memory and 512GB storage to $1,099, and the equivalent 15-inch to $1,299. Last Black Friday, the older M4 models with 256GB reached $749 and $949 respectively. We are already seeing up to $250 off the 1TB models, and $200 off the 512GB options, bringing the price back to the original MSRP before Apple increased prices.  
U.K. Black Friday price: October offers included approximately £1,199 for the 13-inch M5 Air and £1,349 for the 15-inch, both with 512GB storage. Last Black Friday’s M4 models with 256GB reached £849 and £1,025. Match storage capacities when comparing generations. So far in November 2026, we have seen £200 off the 13-inch MacBook Air and £200 off the 15-inch model, which are better than what we saw for Prime Day this October. Now the savings have dropped to a maximum £150 off though.


						

							


MacBook Neo – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




The MacBook Neo suits browsing, schoolwork, streaming, and office apps. Its lower starting price makes it appealing, but its fixed 8GB of memory leaves less room for demanding workloads.
Check which configuration is discounted: only the 512GB version includes Touch ID. Both lack a backlit keyboard, MagSafe, and Thunderbolt. Compare clearance MacBook Air stock before deciding how much those compromises save you.
U.S. Black Friday price: October’s $689 price for the 256GB Neo was only a small reduction from its $699 asking price and the current $13 saving is equally small.
U.K. Black Friday price: We saw a Prime Day low of £549, but that was before Apple increased prices. Now the low is £649, £50 off for the 256GB model. We are also seeing £79 off the 512GB MacBook Neo. 


						

							


MacBook Pro M6 – Best step up from the Air

				
					

				
			
Macbook Pro M6 Aufmacher

Halyna Kubiv




The standard M6 MacBook Pro is worth considering if you want a better built-in display, more connections, and cooling for sustained workloads without paying for a Pro or Max chip. It comes in a 14-inch size, with a non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot.
It starts with 16GB memory and 1TB storage, so account for those specifications when comparing prices with an Air or older Pro. Despite the newer generation number, the standard M6 isn’t automatically the better choice for demanding work than an M5 Pro or M5 Max.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 model wasn’t available during October Prime Day. Its M5 predecessor with 16GB memory and 1TB storage reached $1,839. We aren’t seeing discounts on the M6 yet, but you can get the 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro for $200 less than the new model.
U.K. Black Friday price: Last Black Friday, the older 14-inch M5 with 16GB memory and 1TB storage reached approximately £1,619. We are already seeing £169 off the 14-inch, M6 with 1TB, 16GB, also note that it is only £31.97 more than the M5 (£1,830.97 versus £1,799), so we wouldn’t recommend the older model. 


						

							


MacBook Pro M5 Pro – Best for demanding professional work

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The non-touchscreen M5 Pro MacBook Pro is a strong choice for development, photography, video editing, and heavier multitasking. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, it offers professional performance without the Max chip’s higher price.
Compare it with the touchscreen version using the same memory and storage. Both offer M5 Pro configurations, so a discounted non-touch model could be particularly good value if its existing XDR display meets your needs.
U.S. Black Friday price: October prices included $2,339 for the 14-inch M5 Pro with 24GB memory and 1TB storage, and $2,749 for the equivalent 16-inch. So far this Black Friday month we are seeing $250 off the 16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro, 1TB).
U.K. Black Friday price: The equivalent configurations reached approximately £2,250 and £2,700. Last Black Friday, selected previous-generation M4 Pro models received discounts of around £350. So far this Black Friday there is a £349 saving on the 16-inch M5 Pro model. Note that the 14-inch M5 Pro, 2TB/24GB model is only £24.03 more than the 1TB/24GB version.


						

							


MacBook Pro M5 Max – Best for demanding graphics and video

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




Consider the non-touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work benefits from additional graphics power or more memory than an M5 Pro supports. Complex 3D projects and demanding video production make a stronger case for it than everyday productivity.
We’d choose the configuration around the work you do. A larger advertised discount on a Max doesn’t necessarily make it better value than a less expensive Pro that meets your needs. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the options.
U.S. Black Friday price:  October offers included $3,499 for a 14-inch M5 Max with 2TB storage and $3,899 for a 16-inch with 36GB memory and 2TB storage. Last Black Friday, selected M4 Max configurations were $500 off and this Black Friday month we are already seeing $500 off the M5 Max models. 
U.K. Black Friday price:  October coverage included a 14-inch M5 Max with 2TB storage at £3,799, saving £300. This time there is £100 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Max.


						

							


Touchscreen MacBook Pro – Best for its OLED display

				
					

				
			


Roman Loyola/Foundry




The touchscreen MacBook Pro is most compelling for its OLED display and thinner, lighter design. Improved blacks and reduced blooming could matter more to your everyday experience than touch controls, particularly if you spend most of your working day using the built-in screen.
Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, these models offer comparable processing performance to their non-touch equivalents. Compare matching configurations: the regular premium is $400/£400, so consider how much you’ll benefit from the display before paying extra.
U.S. Black Friday price:  These models arrived in November, so there are no equivalent October Prime Day or Black Friday 2025 prices. Compare any offer with the matching non-touch M5 Pro or M5 Max model. It’s early days so we don’t expect to see big savings here this Black Friday. 
U.K. Black Friday price: In the U.K. we have seen Amazon knock £286 off the price of the MacBook Pro (16-inch, M5 Pro, 1TB, Touchscreen), which helps with affordability for what is a very expensive machine. 


						

							


Mac mini M6 – Our best-value desktop choice

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The M6 Mac mini suits buyers who already own a display, keyboard, and mouse. It offers a compact desktop for everyday work and lighter creative projects. Check storage carefully: the entry-level model has a restrictive 256GB SSD.
U.S. Black Friday price: October’s entry-level M6 mini reached approximately $780. Last Black Friday, the older M4 equivalent was $479. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M6 model reached approximately £824, compared with £499 for the M4 last Black Friday. There’s £100 off the 256GB Mac mini in the U.K.


						

							


Mac mini M5 Pro – Best compact desktop for professional work

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The M5 Pro mini offers more processing power and memory capacity for demanding work without moving to a Studio. Compare upgraded configurations carefully: if the total approaches Mac Studio pricing, check which machine better suits your workload.
U.S. Black Friday price: The 24GB/512GB M5 Pro mini reached approximately $1,550 in October. Last Black Friday’s M4 Pro equivalent was $1,249. So far this November we’ve seen $150 off the 512GB model.
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s M5 Pro configuration reached approximately £1,647. The previous-generation M4 Pro with 24GB/512GB was £1,269 last Black Friday. There is £150 off the 512GB Mac mini M5 Pro in the U.K. 


						

							


iMac – Best complete desktop setup

				
					

				
			

Foundry




The iMac combines a 24-inch 4.5K display with the computer and matching accessories. Compare the two-port and four-port versions carefully: the latter adds processing power, connections, and a Touch ID keyboard. Factor those differences into the final price.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 wasn’t available during October Prime Day. The entry-level M4 predecessor reached approximately $1,360 in October and $1,149 last Black Friday. We’ve not seen any savings yet. 
U.K. Black Friday price: October’s four-port M4 with 256GB storage was £1,620. Last Black Friday, comparable four-port M4 stock reached £1,349. These are predecessor prices rather than M6 targets. The new iMac models aren’t discounted at the moment. 


						

							


Mac Studio – Best for demanding desktop workflows

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




The M5 Max Studio suits demanding graphics, video, and other professional workloads. Compare it with the M5 Pro mini first. The considerably more expensive M5 Ultra is for exceptional workloads requiring its additional performance and memory; most buyers won’t need it. Budget for a display and peripherals.

Should you buy a Mac or MacBook now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need a Mac immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if it matches or approaches a previous low for the same configuration. Waiting can be a gamble if you’re buying clearance stock with a particular screen size, memory capacity, or finish.
The M5 MacBook Air remains an appealing purchase at a good discount, with a replacement not expected until 2027. The recently updated Mac mini and Mac Studio are also worth considering if they meet your needs. The main reason to wait is a better price rather than an imminent replacement.

If your existing M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, there’s little reason to upgrade simply because a newer option exists.
The M6 iMac has only just arrived, replacing the aging M4 version. Compare a modest saving on the latest model with a substantial clearance discount on its predecessor, rather than assuming the older machine is automatically the better deal.
Previous prices need context this year. Following June’s increases, a discount from Apple’s current asking price may still leave you paying more than before the increases. Compare retailers as well: Amazon competes with Best Buy, Walmart, and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys and John Lewis in the U.K. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the current choices.


						

							


Which Mac specifications are worth paying for?
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Use Black Friday to get a configuration that will serve you for longer within your budget, but don’t pay for performance or features you won’t use.
Check the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. A standard M6 and an M5 Pro or M5 Max serve different needs: the newer generation number alone doesn’t tell you which is better for your work. For MacBook Pro listings, distinguish the OLED touchscreen version from non-touch models.
Avoid saving a small amount by buying too little memory or storage. Most current Macs start with 16GB of unified memory, but the MacBook Neo has a fixed 8GB, and some desktop configurations include only a 256GB SSD. Unified memory cannot be upgraded later. An external SSD can add storage, but it cannot compensate for insufficient RAM.
Once the processor meets your needs, additional memory may be more useful than a faster chip. Compare a discounted Air with the Neo, too: the M5 Air starts with twice the memory and storage of the entry-level Neo. Our Mac buying guide explains which specifications suit different workloads.
Check whether the configuration includes nano-texture glass. This optional finish reduces glare and reflections, which can help in bright rooms or near windows, but increases the price. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may offer better value.


						

							


Should you buy an older Mac or MacBook?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older Mac can be excellent value if its price reflects its age and configuration. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of the newer equivalent, rather than focusing on a large percentage saving from its original launch price.
Previous-generation Apple silicon models are the most promising starting point. A discounted M4 MacBook Air or standard M5 MacBook Pro may meet your needs comfortably. Older Pro and Max configurations can also be worth considering if they provide the memory, graphics performance, and connections your work requires for substantially less money.
Check what the saving buys—and what you give up. An older Mac with more memory or storage could be more useful than a newer entry-level configuration. Conversely, a cheaper older Air with 256GB storage isn’t directly comparable with an M5 Air that starts with 512GB. The non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also remain current options, despite the arrival of the standard M6 and touchscreen models.
Be much more cautious with Intel Macs. Their software support is winding down, and a low purchase price may leave you with a machine that has a limited useful life for current apps and macOS features. Check compatibility with the software you need before buying any older model.
For used or refurbished Macs, check battery condition on laptops, warranty coverage, and the returns policy. Confirm that Activation Lock has been removed and that the Mac isn’t still enrolled in an organization’s management system.
For more advice read:
Should I buy a MacBook Neo?
Should I buy a MacBook Air?
Should I buy a MacBook Pro?
Should I buy a Mac mini?
Should I buy a Mac Studio?


						

							


Mac or MacBook deals to avoid
Treat large advertised discounts carefully. Following June’s price increases, “$400 off” may simply bring a Mac closer to what it cost before the increase. Compare previous selling prices for the same configuration, rather than judging the offer solely against today’s recommended price.
Check whether the price includes AppleCare+ or another protection plan. Some Amazon listings bundle coverage with the Mac. If you don’t want it, a listing without coverage could be cheaper; if you do, compare the bundle with buying the Mac and coverage separately.
Check for a bundled power adapter, too. Some Mac laptops are sold without one in the U.K. and EU. A charger bundle may be useful if you need an adapter, but could mean paying extra unnecessarily if you already own a suitable one.
Compare the complete setup cost. A Mac mini or Studio requires a display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad, while adapters and docks can add to the cost of any Mac.
Finally, distinguish cash discounts from gift cards, trade-ins, financing, and membership-only offers. Read the conditions, check the seller, and confirm whether the Mac is new, refurbished, or used, along with its warranty and returns policy.


						

							


How we choose Mac and MacBook deals
Macworld has covered the Mac since its launch in 1984, and our recommendations draw on decades of experience and hands-on reviews. We consider performance, display quality, battery life, portability, connectivity, and everyday use alongside price to explain which Macs suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess which upgrades are worth paying for. We look at whether additional processing power benefits demanding workloads, when more memory is useful, and whether a premium display justifies the extra cost. A MacBook Air may offer better value for everyday work, while a Pro, Max, or Ultra configuration needs to earn its higher price through the work it enables.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than judging a deal solely against today’s recommended retail price. A large advertised discount doesn’t automatically make an offer exceptional.
We consider the complete purchase, too: the retailer, product condition, warranty, and any conditions attached to the price. For desktop Macs, we also account for the display and accessories you’ll need. Our Mac buying guide and MacBook comparison explain how to choose the right model and configuration.
For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our roundups of the best iPad deals, AirPods deals, and Apple Watch deals.

title: Here’s how much you’ll need to pay to use Siri AI after Apple’s new limits kick in
content:
Macworld





Apple Intelligence is a blanket term Apple uses for all sorts of AI features, which are growing in scope and capability with each OS update. Apple has maintained from the start that some of the more advanced features—those that use powerful cloud AI models—will eventually have usage limits.
With the OS 27 software updates and the new features and models available, it’s likely that users are going to run into these limits more often. This Apple Support document describes which features are subject to the Apple Intelligence usage limits. 
Basic Siri commands that happen on your local device, like setting timers or alarms, making a call, texting someone, or opening an app, will always work and do not count toward your cloud usage limits. However, other requests, such as image generation and Siri knowledge, will cost extra if you use them too much. There are four categories:
Siri AI
Intelligent Photo Editing Tools including Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing; and Image Playground generation.
AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro Models in Shortcuts
Developer apps using Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute
Unfortunately, Apple does not publish any specific details on what the limits are. Each of the four categories listed above uses a different amount of your limit with each use, and it’s not clearly stated exactly how much you get or how much each of those features uses. It’s likely that Apple is using the latest iOS betas to gauge the popularity and server load for various features to determine them.
As of iOS 27.3 beta 2, we now have some idea of what happens when you reach your limit and how you can increase it. If you’re using Apple Intelligence a lot on a particular day, you’ll receive a warning pop-up that you are near your daily limit. Once you reach that limit, you’ll be told to either wait for the next daily reset (at midnight local time in most regions) or upgrade your iCloud+ plan to increase your limit.
The increase to your Apple Intelligence cloud usage scales with your iCloud+ plan.


iCloud+ planDaily limit

50 GB ($0.99/month)Standard limit
200 GB ($2.99/month)Up to 2x
2 TB ($9.99/month)Up to 5x
6 TB ($29.99/month)Up to 10x
12 TB ($59.99/month)Up to 20x

 



Each device has its own daily free limit. After that limit is reached, every device signed in to the same Apple Account will draw from a single pool of expanding iCloud+ use. 
If you are using a shared iCloud+ plan (such as an Apple One plan), then any user who reaches their own device’s free use limit will start drawing from that single shared iCloud+ usage limit on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: iPhone Duo guide: Price, specs, availability, problems and reviews
content:
Macworld





Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, brings a larger screen and new ways to use an iPhone – but its launch has also raised questions about durability, app compatibility and availability. We regularly update this guide with the latest reported problems, software updates and app-support developments, alongside pricing, specifications and delivery estimates. Whether you’re considering buying one or already own one, you’ll find the latest developments and advice below.
The Duo went on sale on October 23, 2026, and initial orders quickly pushed delivery estimates into late January. Availability has since begun to improve: when we checked on November 17, Apple listed delivery estimates of December 17–28 in the U.S. and four to five weeks in the U.K. Estimates vary by configuration and location.
Some early owners have reported cracks and bright lines on the inner display. Apple acknowledged an issue affecting a small number of units on October 26 and advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The cause and failure rate remain unclear. Our iPhone Duo problems section explains the reports, Apple’s response and what affected owners should do.
The Duo opens like a book from a 5.4-inch phone into a 7.6-inch device, with a nano-texture inner display, side-button Touch ID and an A20 Pro processor. Software support continues to expand: iOS 27.2 added Apple Pencil (USB-C) support and Edge Light for video calls, while iOS 27.3 beta testing introduces optional front-camera unlocking and Close to Lock. Apple says more than 200,000 apps are now optimized for iPhone Duo, although support varies and some apps still make limited use of its larger display. We track software updates and app compatibility below, explaining what’s available now, what’s being tested and where limitations remain.
iPhone Duo at a glance
Apple’s first folding iPhone, with 5.4-inch outer and 7.6-inch inner displays.
Touch ID replaces Face ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button.
A20 Pro with vapor-chamber cooling, including a new 2nm manufacturing process.
Dual-battery architecture, giving up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display.
Fold-specific iOS and camera features, including Split View, Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and hands-free use.
iPhone Duo: Top 10 features


Foldable designBook-style titanium design with precision hinge
Inner display7.6-inch Super Retina XDR OLED, 120Hz ProMotion
Outer display5.4-inch Super Retina XDR OLED, 120Hz ProMotion
ProcessorA20 Pro, 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU
Neural EngineDual 16-core Neural Engine
AuthenticationTouch ID in side button
Rear cameras48MP Main + 48MP Ultra Wide
BatteryDual batteries; up to 44 hours video on outer screen
ConnectivityC2 modem, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, second-gen UWB
Storage256GB, 512GB, 1TB or 2TB

 






iPhone Duo release date: When did it launch?
Apple announced the iPhone Duo on September 9, 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Sales began on October 23, following preorders on October 16.
The October 23 launch covers more than 70 countries and regions, including the U.S. and U.K., with another 28 markets following on October 30. The Duo will also be available through Apple Stores, selected carriers and authorized retailers, although availability varies by market.
Buy iPhone Duo at Apple U.S. 
Buy iPhone Duo at Apple U.K. 
$1999 at  Apple						
					


						

							


Has the iPhone Duo sold out? 
Initial delivery allocations sold out rapidly, but some new orders are now showing December delivery

				
					

				
			You might be able to get an iPhone Duo by Christmas if you are quick!

Foundry




Delivery estimates have started to improve. By mid-November, some new iPhone Duo orders are showing December 17–28 delivery, rather than late January. Estimates vary by configuration and delivery location, though. 
There are iPhone stock-checking services that may help you locate stock near you. Apple Inventory Check and iPhone Stock Checker monitor Apple Store availability in various countries, including the U.S. and U.K., while TrackaLacker covers selected online retailers, including Best Buy and Walmart. Some notification features require registration or payment.
Apple described preorder demand as “nothing short of extraordinary” and said it was working to get devices to customers as quickly as possible.
Supply constraints may also contribute to the backlog. A late-September report claimed that Apple and its manufacturing partners were experiencing low production yields. Long delivery waits therefore reflect the balance between demand and available supply, rather than revealing how many phones Apple has sold.


						

							


iPhone Duo design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			


Britta O’Boyle/Foundry




The iPhone Duo uses a book-style folding design. Closed, it is unusually short and wide for an iPhone, measuring 84.1mm wide, 117.8mm tall and 11.3mm thick. Open it and the width expands to 164.6mm, while thickness reduces to just 5.2mm, making it Apple’s thinnest iPhone when unfolded (taking that mantle from the iPhone Air). It weighs 254g.
The outer screen measures 5.4 inches, while the folding inner panel measures 7.6 inches. Both are Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz, Always-On display support and up to 3,000 nits outdoor peak brightness. The internal display also has a nano-texture surface designed to reduce reflections and make the crease less noticeable. The inner display also has a replaceable top cover layer. 
According to iFixit’s report on Apple’s U.S. repair pricing, replacing the inner screen’s cover layer costs $49 without AppleCare+, or a $19 service fee with AppleCare+. This replaces only the top cover layer. Repairing damage to the inner display itself costs substantially more: $999 without AppleCare+, or a $99 service fee with AppleCare+. If damage is experienced and found to be a manufacturing fault, Apple may accept the device for repair under warranty at no cost. 
The frame and hinge cover are made from Grade 5 titanium. Apple uses a mirror-polished finish on the enclosure and a micro-blasted finish on the 3D-printed hinge cover. Ceramic Shield protects the rear, while Ceramic Shield 2 protects the outer display. The phone retains an IP68 rating despite its folding construction.

				
					

				
			A closed iPhone Duo.

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry




There are just two colors: Star White and Night Sky, essentially confirming the pre-event reports of silver/white and a very dark blue. For more information read about the iPhone Duo colors.
Action button and Camera Control
There is Camera Control, giving access to exposure, depth, zoom, cameras, styles and tone. It can also launch the new Siri Camera mode.
However, Apple’s Duo doesn’t feature an Action button. The regular iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max retain both the Action button and Camera Control, so this is one hardware-control compromise of the folding model.
Accessories
Apple is also launching two dedicated accessories for the foldable: 
The iPhone Duo Case at $79/£79
The Duo Folio with Kickstand at $129/£129
Apple’s standard case leaves the hinge exposed, while the Folio with Kickstand provides hinge protection.
Both became available to order on October 16. And there are plenty more of the best cases for iPhone Duo in our test reviews.


						

							


iPhone Duo problems: Screen cracks and hinge concerns
Some early iPhone Duo owners have reported cracks along the inner display’s fold, sometimes accompanied by bright lines across the screen. One Australian owner said the damage appeared after around six hours and fewer than 20 openings, and reported receiving an immediate replacement at an Apple Store. These are owner reports; the cause and extent of the problem remain unclear.
Apple acknowledged the issue on October 26, saying it affects a small number of iPhone Duo units. The company advises customers experiencing inner-display problems to contact AppleCare for a replacement. Apple has not announced a formal repair program or confirmed the underlying cause. As reported on November 2, Apple has also circulated diagnostic guidance to Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers. Read our report on the Duo’s display and hinge problems.
iFixit’s teardown offers a possible explanation: its 3D hinge model places reported damage near a transition between the flex-cable opening and central display support. One simulation shows how a support that fails to retract sufficiently could press against the folding screen.
Apple published an iPhone Duo hinge troubleshooting guide on October 23. It covers devices that do not open or close fully, unexpected noises, loose or damaged hinges, and enclosure damage affecting the mechanism.
Apple says there are no software remedies for hinge problems, so restarting, updating or restoring the phone is unnecessary. Its service procedure calls for inspection and, if the problem remains unresolved, replacement of the inner display assembly. Owners experiencing problems should contact Apple or an authorized service provider for assessment.


						

							


How repairable is the iPhone Duo?
iFixit awarded the Duo a provisional repairability score of 5/10, its highest for a foldable at the time. It praised the removable outer display and electrically released batteries, but found inner-display and hinge repairs difficult. The score reflects some accessible components, but is provisional pending replacement-parts availability.
Its fluorescent-powder experiment also found particles reaching the hinge, but this does not establish the cause of owners’ screen failures.


						

							


Face ID, Touch ID and the notch

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle/Foundry




Perhaps the most surprising difference between the iPhone Duo and Apple’s other flagship iPhones is that there is no Face ID.
Instead, Apple has brought back Touch ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button. It works whether the Duo is folded or unfolded, and Apple Watch can also be used to unlock the device. This confirms one of the most persistent pre-launch rumors.
Currently being tested in the iOS 27.3 developer beta 2, a new “Unlock with front camera” option lets you unlock the iPhone Duo while it is closed, provided you have recently authenticated with Touch ID or your passcode. You can enable it in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode. This uses the front camera rather than the TrueDepth system required for Face ID, and only unlocks the phone: Touch ID is still required for Apple Pay and passwords, and again after approximately 45 minutes of inactivity. 
The internal display therefore does not need the TrueDepth sensors used for Face ID. Its FaceTime camera sits beneath the display and disappears when it isn’t being used, giving the inner screen a largely uninterrupted surface.
The inner camera itself is hidden below the display rather than sitting permanently in a visible camera cutout. And yet, despite this and the absence of Face ID, there is still support for Dynamic Island.
Future Duo models could restore Face ID. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple has tested iPhone Duo 2 prototypes with an under-display Face ID sensor and camera on the outer screen. However, he suggests the technology could arrive with either the second or third generation, so its inclusion in the next model remains uncertain.


						

							




iPhone Duo cameras: What cameras does it have?

				
					

				
			
There are two cameras on the rear.

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry




The Duo has a 48MP Dual Fusion camera system, comprising:


CameraResolutionEquivalent focal lengthAperture

Fusion Main48MP26mmf/1.6
2x crop from Main12MP52mmf/1.6
Fusion Ultra Wide48MP13mmf/2.2
Outer front camera12MP—f/2.2
Inner FaceTime cameraApple does not specify resolution—f/1.8

 



The Duo does not have variable aperture. Variable aperture is exclusive to the 48MP Fusion Main camera in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.


The biggest camera features for iPhone Duo
Duo Preview
The outer screen can show a live preview while somebody else is being photographed, allowing the subject to adjust their pose and framing.
Smart Take and Kid Cue
Smart Take detects when everybody is ready and automatically captures the shot. Kid Cue uses animations on the outer screen to encourage children to look towards the camera.
Two-screen shooting
The folding design supports unusual shooting configurations, including using the main cameras for selfies or group photos while seeing the composition on the other screen. Duo FaceTime can also put nearby participants onto the outer display.
Other notable camera features include 48MP macro photography, a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main camera, an under-display inner FaceTime camera, Dual Capture for simultaneous front-and-rear video, and 4K Dolby Vision recording at up to 120fps.


						

							


Rear cameras

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle/Foundry




The 48MP Fusion Main has an f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift stabilization and can shoot 24MP or 48MP images. It also provides a 12MP, 2x optical-quality crop equivalent to a 52mm lens.
The 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide has a 13mm-equivalent lens, f/2.2 aperture and 120-degree field of view. It also supports 48MP macro photography and is the same Ultra Wide camera used by the iPhone 18 Pro family.
That means the Duo does not match the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max camera system. Those phones add a dedicated 48MP Fusion Telephoto and variable aperture on the Main camera, making the Pro models much more flexible for photography despite costing substantially less.
In his first-day testing, Macworld’s Jason Cross found the Duo’s Main camera fell behind the iPhone 18 Pro in low light, although he was pleased with the Ultra Wide camera. The Duo also lacks the Pro’s shutter-speed adjustment and histogram, while retaining white balance and manual focus with focus peaking.
Pre-event reports were divided between a Main + Telephoto and Main + Ultra Wide arrangement. Apple ultimately chose Main + Ultra Wide, confirming the earlier reports that a dedicated telephoto could be sacrificed to save space.
Front cameras
On the outside is a 12MP Center Stage camera with an f/2.2 aperture. It supports Center Stage, automatic portrait/landscape framing, Dual Capture, Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5 and 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 60fps.
Inside is an under-display FaceTime camera with an f/1.8 aperture. Apple does not specify its megapixel resolution. It supports Center Stage for video calls and records at up to 1080p/60fps. Its major advantage is visual rather than photographic: the camera effectively disappears beneath the display when it isn’t being used.
However, image quality is a compromise. In Macworld’s testing, we found that the under-display camera produced poor detail and dynamic range. It is adequate for video calls, but for better selfies, it’s preferable to use the rear cameras with the outer display as a viewfinder.
iPhone Duo video features
The Main camera records 4K Dolby Vision at 24, 25, 30, 60, 100 or 120fps, with 4K/120fps also available for slo-mo. Cinematic mode reaches 4K/60fps and Action mode up to 2.8K/60fps. Dual Capture can record at up to 4K/30fps.
Apple’s specifications also do not list ProRes or Apple Log recording for the Duo. Those remain more Pro-oriented capabilities rather than part of Apple’s foldable camera proposition.
The Duo does support Spatial Audio recording, Audio Mix, Dolby Vision HDR and Apple’s computational photography features including Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5, Photographic Styles 3, smart focus tracking and Apple Intelligence-powered editing.
Apple does not list conventional Spatial Video capture in the Duo specifications.


						

							


iPhone Duo processor: What processor does it use?

				
					

				
			
Watch video on the screen.

Apple




The iPhone Duo uses the A20 Pro, the same processor as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, a major step forward in transistor density and efficiency. Apple combines it with a new chip packaging design inspired by its M-series Mac processors. The package connects the A20 Pro directly to a custom vapor chamber to transfer heat away from the processor more effectively.
The A20 Pro includes:
6-core CPU: two super cores and four efficiency cores
7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators
Dual 16-core Neural Engine
Hardware-accelerated ray tracing
A dedicated display engine capable of operating both Duo displays
Compared with the A19 Pro, Apple says the CPU is up to 20 percent faster, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power-efficient. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers twice the compute power, while unified-memory bandwidth rises by 50 percent.
Apple also claims that the complete thermal system gives the Duo up to 35 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. That sustained-performance figure is particularly important for a folding device because prolonged gaming, multitasking and AI workloads generate considerably more heat than short benchmark bursts.


						

							


iPhone Duo RAM: How much memory does it have?
Apple has not disclosed how much RAM is inside the iPhone Duo.
Before launch, supply-chain reports consistently pointed to 12GB of RAM, which would make sense given the demands of running two displays, simultaneous applications, Siri AI and larger on-device AI models. 
Apple does reveal that A20 Pro has 50 percent more unified-memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, which should help the Duo move data more quickly between the CPU, GPU and Neural Engine.
Extra memory is particularly useful on the Duo because iOS 27.1 can display multiple apps simultaneously and because Apple Intelligence and Siri AI increasingly run generative models locally rather than relying entirely on cloud processing.


						

							


iPhone Duo connectivity

				
					

				
			
Folded iPhone Duo. 

Britta O’Boyle




Apple has put a significant amount of its own communications silicon into the iPhone Duo.
It uses Apple’s new C2 cellular modem, replacing Qualcomm silicon. Apple says C2 introduces AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability and supports mmWave 5G in the U.S.
The N1 wireless networking chip provides:
Wi-Fi 7 with 2×2 MIMO
Bluetooth 6
Thread networking
The USB-C port also supports USB 3 data transfers at up to 10Gbps and DisplayPort video output.
The Duo also has Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, NFC and precision dual-frequency GPS.
It is eSIM-only worldwide, something that had been widely rumored before launch. Eliminating the SIM tray gives Apple additional internal space for its batteries.
iPhone Handoff – a feature introduced with iOS 27 – makes it easier to use an iPhone Duo alongside another iPhone without needing separate phone numbers. Both devices share your number, with calls, voicemail, messages and Find My location following whichever iPhone you unlock. Only one phone is active at a time. You could use the Duo’s folding display for work, then switch to an iPhone Pro when you want its telephoto camera. Both phones need iOS 27, eSIM support and the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled. Your carrier must specifically support iPhone Handoff, and your plan may require an additional monthly fee for access. T-Mobile already offers iPhone Handoff for $5 a month; Verizon and EE (in the U.K.) plan support. Fees may apply.
Satellite capabilities include:
Emergency SOS via satellite
Roadside Assistance via satellite
Find My via satellite
Messages via satellite


						

							


Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s available?
Instead of one battery spanning the body, the iPhone Duo contains two rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, with one high-energy battery fitted into each half of the device. Apple’s energy-balancing algorithms make them operate as a single battery system.
Apple rates battery life at:
Up to 24 hours of typical use
Up to 44 hours video playback using the outer display
Up to 31 hours using the inner display
Up to 37 hours streamed video on the outer screen
Up to 26 hours streamed video on the inner display
Early reviewers reported different battery experiences. CNET found the Duo comfortably lasted through a busy day, while The Verge questioned whether it could manage a full day of heavy use. These observations reflect different usage patterns and testing methods, so they should not be treated as directly comparable results or replacements for Apple’s playback ratings above.
After using the Duo as her main phone for a week, Macworld contributor Britta O’Boyle generally finished her mixed-use days with around 25 percent battery remaining. In her experience, it outlasted the smaller iPhone 18 Pro but fell slightly short of the Pro Max. These are everyday-use observations rather than directly comparable laboratory benchmarks.
Apple has not disclosed the batteries’ combined capacity in mAh. The pre-launch rumor of approximately 5,000-5,500mAh therefore remains unconfirmed.
Apple says the iPhone Duo can reach 50 percent charge in around 20 minutes using a USB-C charging cable and a 60W-capable power adapter or higher.
Britta O’Boyle’s charging test broadly matched Apple’s claim: using a 60W adapter, she reached approximately 50 percent from empty in around 20 minutes.
Our iPhone Duo reviewer, Jason Cross, found that battery life depended heavily on which display he used. Frequent gaming or video editing on the inner screen could require charging by mid-afternoon, while more folded use left plenty of charge at bedtime. Unfortunately, Macworld’s standard battery benchmark app crashed on launch, so his review contains no directly comparable laboratory battery result.
MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging are supported at up to 25W. Apple’s claimed 50 percent charge in around 30 minutes requires a MagSafe charger paired with a 35W-or-higher power adapter.
In both the U.S. and U.K., the box includes the iPhone Duo and a 1-meter USB-C charging cable, but no power adapter. The MagSafe charger is also sold separately, so factor these accessories into your budget if you don’t already own suitable equipment.


						

							




iPhone Duo price: How much does it cost?
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 in the U.S. and £1,999 in the U.K. for 256GB.
Prices are:


StoragePrice

256GB$1,999/£1,999
512GB$2,199/£2,199
1TB$2,599/£2,599
2TB$3,199/£3,199

 



The 256GB starting capacity means Apple has not created an unusually low-storage entry model simply to make the headline price look lower.


iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro pricing
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. That makes the Duo approximately $700/£700 more expensive than the Pro Max at entry level.
That premium buys the folding display, precision hinge, titanium structure, second screen and more complex dual-battery design rather than superior cameras: in several areas the iPhone 18 Pro models are actually better equipped.
Reports before the launch suggested the Duo could cost anywhere from around $1,999 to $2,399 at entry level, largely because of the folding OLED display, hinge mechanism, titanium components and other expensive parts. Apple ultimately landed at the very bottom of those predictions.


						

							


iPhone Duo software: Multitasking and Apple Pencil support

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle





The iPhone Duo’s larger inner display enables Split View, letting you use two apps side by side. For example, you could keep Safari open while taking notes, or check your calendar alongside a conversation in Messages. Supported apps can also open two windows of their own: Safari can display two webpages side by side for comparison shopping. You can save pairs of apps to return to later.
App compatibility varies considerably. Macworld’s Jason Cross identified three broad experiences: older apps with fixed layouts and black borders; apps updated for iOS 27 that resize across the displays; and fully Duo-optimized apps that adapt to its different positions. After some initial issues, Outlook has been updated and now has a Duo-optimized layout that makes better use of the inner display.
App support is improving. On November 16, Apple’s marketing chief Greg Joswiak said more than 200,000 apps were now optimized for iPhone Duo. Netflix, Fantastical, MLB and Asphalt Legends were among the apps Apple highlighted at launch, and optimized apps carry a “Made for iPhone Duo” badge on their App Store product pages.
However, the growing number of optimized apps does not guarantee that your essential apps make full use of the Duo’s displays and different positions. Before buying, check the apps you rely on. The crowdsourced Works on Duo database can help you see how individual apps use its screens.
StandBy also works differently on the Duo. Set the phone down and it can display a clock, photos or widgets on either screen without being connected to a charger. New Calendar and Weather faces join the existing options.
Apple Pencil (USB-C) support arrived with iOS 27.2 on October 26, allowing users to write, sketch and mark up documents on either display. Update through Settings > General > Software Update to access the feature.
The update also adds Edge Light, which uses the display to illuminate your face during video calls. Other iOS 27.2 additions include improvements to Siri AI’s conversation recall and personal context, plus contextual Suggestions in Messages. Read our guide to the iOS 27.2 update.
New options being tested in iOS 27.3
Developer beta 2, currently being tested, introduces front-camera unlocking and an optional Close to Lock setting. Front-camera unlocking is enabled through Settings > Touch ID & Passcode, subject to the authentication restrictions explained above. Close to Lock, found in Settings > Display & Brightness, lets you choose to lock the Duo when you fold it shut. 


						

							


iPhone Duo review: What did Macworld think?
In Macworld’s full iPhone Duo review, Jason Cross praises the nano-texture inner display, fast performance and thoughtful layouts in optimized apps. 
However, many everyday apps remain awkward to use, while the cameras and Touch ID introduce further compromises. 
Our verdict: An exciting device to explore, but one he cannot yet recommend buying.


						

							


Should you buy the iPhone Duo?

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle




Our advice is to wait, principally because too many popular apps still work poorly on the Duo. Before buying an iPhone Duo, check whether the apps you rely on have layouts designed for its displays.
Additionally, at $1,999/£1,999 it is enormously expensive, and there are significant compromises: no Face ID, no dedicated telephoto camera, no variable aperture and no Action button. 
Durability is another consideration. On October 26, Apple acknowledged an inner-display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units and advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The cause and failure rate remain unclear. If first-generation reliability concerns you, consider waiting for further investigation and longer-term testing before spending $1,999/£1,999.
For photography, battery life and conventional everyday use, the better-value iPhone 18 Pro Max is the best iPhone.
Also read: When is the best time to buy an iPhone and our iPhone Buying Guide.

title: iPhone Duo 2 rumored to get Face ID, but other upgrades will need to wait
content:
Macworld





Mark Gurman’s latest Power On newsletter is mostly about Apple’s upcoming smart glasses, but it does have one interesting bit of iPhone Duo 2 information in it.
Apple has been aware that the missing Face ID is an issue since before the device launched, and has been working on adding it to the second-gen version. According to Gurman, the company  has iPhone Duo 2 with Face ID in prototype form, but the design is not finalized. And they’re running out of time—in order to get iPhone Duo 2 on shelves in the fall of 2027, the design needs to be finalized soon, so they can start building test units, fixing problems, and lining up all the supply they need before starting the full production run in the summer.
The other priority for Apple is to add the Action button, also missing from iPhone Duo. It is possible that Apple will combine its function with the Camera button (also seldom used), as some rumors have suggested.
All the other complaints about iPhone Duo are going to have to wait. There isn’t enough time to incorporate user feedback into the design of the iPhone Duo 2, but Apple’s further-out priorities, according to Gurman, are adding a telephoto camera and making the device thinner and lighter. So if you’re hoping for an iPhone Duo that’s closer to the iPhone Pro’s design, it looks like you’ll be waiting until at least 2028.
It’s likely that Apple wants to improve the hinge mechanism as well. The current design uses a hinge made from 116 parts, which is a manufacturing challenge. Making the hinge simpler without sacrificing quality would reduce manufacturing costs and improve reliability.
